docs.title: Stake Athletics Committee — Detailed Charter and Meeting Plan
docs.text: Companion document to the Boise Idaho YSA Stake Comprehensive Gathering Plan and the Stake YSA Council Charter and Meeting Plan. Prepared for the Boise Idaho YSA Stake YSA Council — October 2026.

docs.title: 1. Purpose of This Document
docs.text:
The Gathering Plan identifies Stake Athletics as one of three ways the stake reaches young single adults, alongside Stake Activities and Education & Enrichment. The Stake YSA Council Charter then hands ownership of the athletics piece to a pair of Athletics Committee Co-Chairs on the Stake YSA Council.

This charter turns that assignment into something you can run with day to day. It outlines how the Athletics Committee is structured and staffed, and who's responsible for planning and running every open-play night, league season, tournament, and inter-stake event described in Part 3 of the Gathering Plan. The Gathering Plan sets out what athletics needs to accomplish; this document specifies who does it, how many people it takes, how the work is split across sports and seasons, and how the Committee keeps the stake presidency in the loop through the Stake YSA Council.

Athletics Co-Chairs should use this as their working playbook and onboarding guide, following the same format as the Stake YSA Council Charter and Meeting Plan.

docs.title: 2. Who's Responsible for What
docs.text:
The Gathering Plan and the Stake YSA Council Charter draw a clear line between deciding and doing. This charter keeps that same line for athletics:

Group What They Do Stake Presidency Sets the overall vision for YSA athletics through the Gathering Plan, and signs off on this charter and any major changes. Calls and releases the Athletics Co-Chairs, based on a recommendation from the YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs. Approves the yearly athletics budget, facility priorities, and any spending outside the plan. Steps in on building-use conflicts, safety issues, and sensitive personal situations that get referred up through the Council. Stake YSA Council Holds the Athletics Committee accountable, the same way it does for Activities and Education & Enrichment. Gets a monthly report from the Athletics Co-Chairs and rolls it into the Council's overall report to the stake presidency. Settles calendar conflicts between Athletics, Activities, and Education & Enrichment. Stake Athletics Committee Fully owns the running of the athletics side of the Gathering Plan, including open play, stake leagues, tournaments, and inter-stake events. Builds and runs the season calendar, staffs every sport and event, tracks weekly turnout and outreach, and adjusts on the fly. Manages the approved athletics budget and oversees Sport Commissioners, Team Captains, Connection Hosts, and the Facility & Equipment Steward. Reports progress, risks, and needs to the Stake YSA Council on a regular schedule (Section 7).

What the Committee can decide on its own:

  • Season format, which sports to run, and the monthly/quarterly calendar, as long as it fits the four stake priorities.
  • How teams are formed, roster rules, and mixing players across wards.
  • Day-to-day officiating, schedule tweaks, and mid-season roster changes.

Check in with the Stake YSA Council or stake presidency before:

  • Calling, releasing, or changing anyone on the Athletics Committee.
  • Spending beyond the approved budget, or adding a sport or tournament that isn't already on the calendar.
  • Facility conflicts with priesthood meetings or other stake/ward activities.
  • For safety incidents, injuries requiring medical attention, or sensitive personal situations, send these directly to the bishops or the stake presidency rather than handling them within the Committee.

docs.title: 3. How the Committee Is Organized
docs.text: The Athletics Committee is organized in three parts to maintain clear accountability: two Co-Chairs who own the results, a group that runs each sport and season, and a ward-level network that delivers invitations and follow-up to every ward.

docs.title: 3.1 Committee Leadership — Co-Chairs
docs.text:
Two seats, filled by young single adults, who jointly own the whole athletics side of the Gathering Plan, matching Section 4.7–4.8 of the Stake YSA Council Charter:

Seat # Seats What They Do Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood, YSA High Councilor) 1 Co-leads athletics with Sister Co-Chair; season calendar, facility scheduling, safety standards, and the "More Than a Game" spiritual message Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Sister) 1 Co-leads athletics with the Priesthood Co-Chair; makes sure sisters feel included in athletics; coordinates outreach with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads

Two people total, and both also sit on the Stake YSA Council.

docs.title: 3.2 Running Each Sport
docs.text:
As described in Part 3 of the Gathering Plan, each season's sports are staffed by Sport Commissioners, Team Captains, and Connection Hosts, plus one Facility & Equipment Steward who stays in place year-round:

Seat Name # Seats What They Do Sport Commissioner (one per active sport) TBD (rotating by season) 4–6 Handles scheduling, rules, equipment, and officiating for one sport during its season Team Captain (one per team) TBD (rotating by season) 8–12 Looks after one team, attendance, following up with people who miss, and taking turns with the spiritual thought Connection Host (Athletics) TBD (rotating) 2 per night Greets and welcomes newcomers at open-play and tournament nights Facility & Equipment Steward TBD 1 Building access, equipment inventory, and first aid/safety

docs.title: 3.3 Ward-Level Support — Rep A & Rep B
docs.text: Athletics doesn't add a new ward calling. As outlined in the Stake YSA Council Charter (§4.14, Ward Representatives), each ward's two Ward Representatives: the Counselor in the Ward Elders Quorum Presidency (Representative A) and the Counselor in the Ward Relief Society Presidency (Representative B) serve as the Ward Athletics Representatives for their respective organizations. They bring the Athletics Committee's work to that ward by inviting people, tracking attendance at athletic events, and following up with newcomers and those who missed out within 48 hours. Ward Athletics Representatives are part of the YSA Council and attend the monthly Stake YSA Council meeting, bringing stake-level assignments back to their ward.

docs.title: 3.4 Married Couple Advisors
docs.text: Following the Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise YSA Stake, married couples serve as mentors and role models rather than as managers. They show up, offer encouragement, and share what they've learned. They don't plan, run, or referee in place of a YSA leader.

docs.title: 3.5 How Big the Committee Gets
docs.text:
Add it up: 2 Co-Chairs + 4–6 Sport Commissioners + 8–12 Team Captains (in-season) + a rotating group of Connection Hosts + 1 Facility & Equipment Steward.

Wards in Stake Sports at Once Team Captains Co-Chairs Total Roster 6 4–6 8–12 2 Roughly 16–20, standing plus rotating

Keep the Co-Chairs seats at two — that's the same clear-accountability model the Stake YSA Council Charter uses for every part of the Gathering Plan.

docs.title: 4. What Each Role Does
docs.text: Each role below is spelled out so you can hand it straight to someone when you call or brief them.

docs.title: 4.1 Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Reports to: YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-chairs the committee with the Sister Co-Chair, and oversees the Sport Commissioners, Team Captains, and Connection Hosts.
  • Owns facility scheduling, equipment inventory, and safety standards for all athletics.
  • Builds and runs the season calendar (open play, leagues, tournaments, inter-stake and outdoor events) and gets it to the Communications & Calendar Lead at least 60 days ahead.
  • Makes sure every league and open-play night includes the "More Than a Game" spiritual message and the written sportsmanship standard.
  • Recruits, briefs, and checks in with Sport Commissioners each season, and represents the Committee at the Stake YSA Council meeting.

What it looks like when it's working

attendance trending up week over week; absentees contacted within 48 hours; seasons starting on time.

docs.title: 4.2 Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Reports to: YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-chairs the committee with the Priesthood Co-Chair, sharing full ownership of the calendar and program quality.
  • Makes sure every league, open-play night, and tournament is designed so everyone feels included, welcome, and belongs.
  • Works with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads to make sure less-active and new-move-in YSAs get personally invited.
  • Coordinates recruiting and training Connection Hosts with the Ward Athletics Representatives.
  • Tracks weekly attendance, absentee follow-up, and less-active/non-member turnout alongside the Priesthood Co-Chair.

What success looks like

How many 48-hour follow-ups actually happen, and how many newcomers come back.

docs.title: 4.3 Sport Commissioner (one per sport, per season)
docs.text:
Reports to: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs

  • Owns scheduling, rules, equipment, and officiating for one sport during its season: volleyball, basketball, futsal, softball, pickleball, flag football, or ultimate frisbee.
  • Recruits and briefs Team Captains for that sport, and makes sure teams are mixed across wards so people aren't just playing with the same ward crowd.
  • Works with the Facility & Equipment Steward on reservations and makes sure scheduling respects the Sabbath.
  • Runs the season opener and closer, including the stake tournament at the end.
  • Reports weekly attendance, any incidents, and roster changes to the Committee Secretary.

What it looks like when it's working

the season starts and ends on time; facility and officiating problems get fixed the same week.

docs.title: 4.4 Team Captain
docs.text:
Reports to: Sport Commissioner (functionally)

  • Looks out for teammates, not just plays with them: knows everyone's name, tracks attendance, and reaches out to anyone who misses within 48 hours.
  • Welcomes non-members, investigators, and less-active YSAs onto the team, no exceptions.
  • Pairs up active YSAs with less-active or new teammates ("Adopt a Player").
  • Leads a short prayer and a spiritual thought when a Commissioner or Connection Host isn't present.
  • Reports attendance and follow-up needs to the Sport Commissioner after each game.

What it looks like when it's working

team attendance trending up; most absentees contacted within 48 hours.

docs.title: 4.5 Connection Host (Athletics)
docs.text:
Reports to: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs (functionally); on-site Sport Commissioner

  • Greets people at every open-play, league, and tournament night, finds whoever's standing alone, and learns their name.
  • Encourages people to bring a friend, and welcomes newcomers, investigators, and less-active YSAs.
  • Leads the pre-game prayer and spiritual thought when no Commissioner is around.
  • Passes the names of newcomers and absentees to the appropriate Team Captain or Sport Commissioner for follow-up within 48 hours.

What it looks like when it's working

newcomers greeted and remembered by name each night; follow-up actually happens.

docs.title: 4.6 Facility & Equipment Steward
docs.text:
Reports to: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs

  • Handles building access, court and field reservations, and keeps scheduling Sabbath-respectful across wards.
  • Keeps the shared equipment inventory up to date, and hands out and collects gear each season.
  • Owns first aid kits, injury procedures, concussion awareness, and any liability/release forms.
  • Brings unresolved facility conflicts to the Priesthood Co-Chair to sort out with bishops.

What it looks like when it's working

no facility conflicts left unresolved; equipment inventory is accurate; every safety incident gets logged and closed.

docs.title: 4.7 Ward Athletics Representatives (Rep A & Rep B)
docs.text:
Reports to: Athletics Co-Chairs (day-to-day); ward bishopric liaison (for pastoral matters)

  • These are the ward's existing Ward Representatives (§4.14 of the Stake YSA Council Charter) — the Counselor in the Ward Elders Quorum Presidency (Representative A) and the Counselor in the Ward Relief Society Presidency (Representative B) — no separate calling needed.
  • Each promotes athletics within their respective organization and personally invites people to open play, leagues, and tournaments.
  • Tracks the ward's athletics attendance alongside activities and enrichment for their organization, and follows up with that organization's newcomers and absentees within 48 hours.
  • Attends the monthly Stake YSA Council meeting and flags any facility, safety, or participation concerns to the Athletics Co-Chairs.

What it looks like when it's working

ward-level attendance trending up; follow-up actually gets done.

docs.title: 4.8 Married Couple Advisors
docs.text:
Reports to: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs (as mentors, not managers)

  • Show up to open-play nights, league games, and tournaments as guests and friends are present, not running things per the stake's married-couple guidance.
  • Offer experience and encouragement to Sport Commissioners and Team Captains when asked or prompted. Never plan, run, or referee in place of a YSA leader.
  • Model "connection before competition" and the adult-to-adult boundaries laid out in A Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise Idaho YSA Stake.
  • Coordinate who attends when with the Priesthood Co-Chair.

What it looks like when it's working

consistent attendance at league nights; Co-Chairs feel coached, not managed.

docs.title: 5. How People Are Chosen, and For How Long
docs.text:
Seat How They're Chosen Term Athletics Co-Chairs The Co-Chair (priesthood) is a YSA High Councilor. The Co-Chair (sister) is nominated by the YSA Council. The sister Co-Chair, along with the stake presidency, is extended as a calling ("Stake YSA Athletics Committee Co-Chair"), interviewed, and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered Sport Commissioners Nominated by the Co-Chairs each season; assigned or called depending on how long the season runs. One season (6–8 weeks) up to a full year for the flagship winter sport Team Captains Picked by the Sport Commissioner from the team roster, favoring YSAs who haven't led before. One season Connection Hosts Recruited by the Co-Chairs or Commissioners from anyone willing, including people building confidence with a first calling. Rotating, night by night or season by season Facility & Equipment Steward Nominated by the Priesthood Co-Chair; extended as a calling or formal assignment. 12–18 months Ward Athletics Representatives Already serving as Ward Representatives — Elders Quorum Presidency Counselor (Rep A) and Relief Society Presidency Counselor (Rep B); no separate calling. Same as their existing calling Married Couple Advisors Assigned by the stake presidency. Ongoing, reviewed annually

Stagger terms so that no more than half the Sport Commissioners turn over at once between seasons. When the calendar allows, build in a 2–3-week overlap between an outgoing and incoming Commissioner or Captain — YSA turnover is naturally high, so this overlap helps.

docs.title: 6. Season Calendar and Levels of Play
6.1 The Three Levels of Play
docs.text:
Athletics runs three levels of the same on-ramp described in Part 3 of the Gathering Plan: connection before competition, regular touchpoints, and a Christ-centered message at every level.

Level What It Looks Like Open Play Nights (Easiest to Join) Drop in anytime — no roster, no commitment, no skill needed; teams get formed on the spot each week. Happens weekly or every other week, rotating through basketball, volleyball, pickleball, and futsal. A Connection Host greets newcomers, learns their names, and personally invites them to the next event or institute. Stake Leagues (Building Real Connection) Structured 6–8 week seasons that end in a stake tournament and social. Teams are deliberately mixed across wards so people aren't stuck with the same ward group; each team has a Team Captain. Inter-Stake and Regional Events (Growing the Network) Inter-stake basketball tournament, regional softball invitational, combined outdoor adventure events, and YSA sports festivals. Great chances to build friendships and, even eternal relationships and marriages.

docs.title: 6.2 The Yearly Schedule
docs.text:
The Athletics Co-Chairs send this calendar to the Communications & Calendar Lead at least 60 days before each season starts, matching the Stake YSA Council's master calendar standard.

Season Sports Notes Fall Volleyball and flag football leagues start; open play resumes Kicks off with the Fall Kickoff Social and the new-move-in welcome Winter Basketball (the flagship league) and futsal; weekly open-play Monthly "More Than a Game" devotional; push for winter institute enrollment Spring Pickleball and softball leagues start; basketball tournaments wrap up Timed with the Easter-season fireside and temple recommend campaign Summer Coed softball, ultimate frisbee, and tournament season Outdoor adventure crossover with Stake Activities; inter-stake tournament

docs.title: 7. How We Meet and Report Back
docs.text: Meeting Frequency Who's There What It's For Athletics Committee Meeting Weekly in season, every other week off-season Co-Chairs, Sport Commissioners, Facility & Equipment Steward Prayer and a spiritual thought for specific YSAs; review the week's attendance and follow-up; sort out facility and equipment issues Team Captain / Connection Host Huddle Weekly, in-season Sport Commissioner, Team Captains, Connection Hosts for that sport Confirm rosters, who's following up with absentees, and whose turn it is for the spiritual thought Stake YSA Council Meeting Monthly Athletics Co-Chairs, other Leads, and Ward Representatives Coordinate the calendar across all three channels; cross-ward invitations; hear back from the wards Stake YSA Council Stewardship Report Monthly Athletics Co-Chairs and the Committee Secretary The athletics section of the combined monthly report to the stake presidency Quarterly Priority Review Quarterly Athletics Co-Chairs, Stake YSA Council, Stake Presidency A deeper look at attendance and outreach against the four stake priorities

docs.title: 7.1 How Information Flows Up
docs.text:
Information and accountability move in one clear line, so nothing gets lost between the game floor and the stake presidency:

  1. Team Captains and Connection Hosts track and report attendance, contacts, and follow-up at every game and open-play night.
  2. Sport Commissioners pull that data together by sport and bring it to the Athletics Committee Meeting.
  3. The Athletics Co-Chairs combine all of it into the athletics section of the monthly report.
  4. The Committee Secretary folds the athletics report into the Stake YSA Council's overall monthly report to the stake presidency.

docs.title: 7.2 What Goes in the Monthly Report
docs.text:
Each month, the Athletics Co-Chairs write this section for the Committee Secretary to add to the Stake YSA Council's combined report. It follows the same format as the Gathering Plan's measurement framework (Part 3, Section 7):

  • Participation — weekly attendance by sport, compared to last month and to the roster.
  • Outreach — less-active and non-member attendance; absentee contacts made within 48 hours.
  • Covenant Progression — people moving from open play to league to institute to temple night.
  • Look-Ahead — what's coming in the next 60 days and what support is needed.
  • Risks, Needs & Decisions Requested — facility, equipment, safety, or staffing items that need a decision from the Stake YSA Council or stake presidency.

docs.title: 8. Who Decides What
docs.text: Decision Athletics Committee Stake Presidency / Committee Season calendar, format, and sport selection Decides Informed Team formation and roster rules Decides Informed New sport, tournament, or spending beyond approved budget Recommends Approves Extending or releasing a Commissioner, Captain, or Steward Recommends Approves and sets apart (for callings) Facility scheduling or conflicts Coordinates Resolves conflicts Safety incidents or sensitive personal situations Flags immediately Handles with bishops

docs.title: 9. Safety and Equipment Basics
docs.text:
• Facilities — coordinated access to stake and ward buildings; respecting priesthood-occupied spaces; scheduling around the Sabbath.
  • Safety — first aid kits at every game and open-play night; injury procedures and concussion awareness; liability/release forms where needed.
  • Sportsmanship — a written standard that emphasizes respect, inclusion, and Christlike conduct; no ejections, conflicts resolved with grace.
  • Cost — kept low, with a scholarship or subsidy available so no one is left out for financial reasons.
  • Equipment — a shared stake supply kept up by the Facility & Equipment Steward, with Sport Commissioners keeping their own sport's inventory.

docs.title: 10. How We Operate
docs.text:
• Every meeting, practice, and game begins and ends with prayer and a short spiritual thought tied to one of the four stake priorities — the "More Than a Game" standard.
  • Connection comes before competition; winning matters less than belonging, from open play all the way to the stake tournament.
  • Conversations about specific people (absentee outreach, sensitive needs) stay within the Committee and are only shared with bishops when they truly need to know.
  • Decisions are made by consensus between the Co-Chairs and the relevant Commissioners; if something can't be resolved, it goes to the YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs within a week rather than sitting unsettled.
  • Sport Commissioners are expected at the Athletics Committee Meeting. If a Commissioner can't make it, a Team Captain fills in.
  • Married Couple Advisors come as guests and friends, not staff, per the stake's married-couple guide; they let YSA leaders greet, run, and close things out.
  • Every Committee member adheres to the same idea the Gathering Plan uses everywhere: this is an on-ramp, not a destination.

docs.title: 11. Bringing New People Up to Speed
docs.text:
• New Athletics Committee members get an onboarding packet: this charter, the relevant part of the Gathering Plan, the current participation numbers, and a handoff document from whoever had the role before them.
  • New Sport Commissioners shadow the outgoing Commissioner for a full season before taking over fully, whenever the timing allows.
  • Each Commissioner maintains a running handoff document, facility contacts, equipment inventory, open items, and lessons learned, updated continuously, not just at the end.
  • Team Captains and Connection Hosts get briefed by their Sport Commissioner within a week of starting, covering how invitations work, follow-up expectations, and the sportsmanship standard.
  • Married Couple Advisors review A Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise YSA Stake before their first season.

docs.title: 12. First 90 Days
docs.text:
Timeframe What Happens Weeks 1–2 Co-Chairs confirm this charter with the Stake YSA Council, check the athletics roster, and identify Sport Commissioner candidates for the next season. Weeks 2–4 Sport Commissioners and the Facility & Equipment Steward are called or assigned; ward bishoprics are reminded that both Ward Representatives (Rep A and Rep B) cover Ward Athletics for their respective organizations. Weeks 4–6 First Athletics Committee Meeting; season calendar published to the Communications & Calendar Lead; equipment inventory confirmed. Weeks 6–8 Team Captains and Connection Hosts recruited and briefed; open-play nights and league play begin; facility reservations confirmed with bishops. Weeks 8–12 The first monthly athletics report goes to the Committee Secretary; the first "More Than a Game" devotional is held; the first quarterly review is scheduled.

This follows the same timing as Phase 1 and the start of Phase 2 of the Gathering Plan, and the Stake YSA Councils Charter's own First 90 Days checklist — so Athletics moves on the same clock as the rest of the Stake YSA Council.

docs.title: 13. Summary
docs.text: This charter establishes a Stake Athletics Committee for the Boise Idaho YSA Stake, run entirely by young single adults and co-led by a YSA High Councilor and a Sister Co-Chair who share full responsibility for the athletics side of the Gathering Plan. It staffs every sport and season through Sport Commissioners, Team Captains, Connection Hosts, and a Facility & Equipment Steward, and reaches every ward through the existing Ward Representative Network without adding a new calling. A regular meeting rhythm and a clear reporting line keep the Stake YSA Council and the stake presidency informed and able to guide the vision. Meanwhile, married-couple advisors mentor from beside the court, not from a position of authority. The result: connection before competition, and every open-play night, league game, and tournament remains what the Gathering Plan intends it to be, an on-ramp on the path to covenants, not a final destination.

docs.title: Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Committee Leadership — paired calling

  • Reports To: YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs; also sits on the Stake YSA Council.
  • Positions Needed: One (YSA High Councilor)

Purpose

Stake Athletics is one of the three ways the Gathering Plan reaches young single adults, alongside Stake Activities and Learning & Enrichment. The Priesthood Co-Chair jointly owns that entire piece with the Sister Co-Chair — the calendar, the facilities, the safety standards, and ensuring that connection comes before competition at every open-play night, league, and tournament.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-chairs the committee with the Sister Co-Chair, and oversees the Sport Commissioners, Team Captains, and Connection Hosts.
  • Owns facility scheduling, equipment inventory, and safety standards for all athletics.
  • Builds and runs the season calendar (open play, leagues, tournaments, inter-stake and outdoor events) and gets it to the Communications & Calendar Lead at least 60 days ahead.
  • Makes sure every league and open-play night includes the "More Than a Game" spiritual message and the written sportsmanship standard.
  • Recruits, briefs, and checks in with Sport Commissioners each season, and represents the Committee at the Stake YSA Council meeting.

Implementation Ideas

  • Build a rolling season-calendar template and lock it in 60+ days out, every season, before sending it to the Communications & Calendar Lead.
  • Open every Committee meeting, league night, and open-play with the same short prayer plus a 60–90 second spiritual thought, rotating who gives it, so "More Than a Game" never gets skipped when things get busy.
  • Keep a shared facility/equipment tracker with the Steward and flag Sabbath-scheduling conflicts before they reach the bishops.
  • When recruiting a Sport Commissioner, walk through purpose, time commitment, training, and who they report to before asking them to accept — the same pattern the General Handbook uses for extending a calling.
  • Hold a short weekly huddle with the Sister Co-Chair during season to compare notes before the full Committee meets.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §4.1, §7, §10; Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §1–3; General Handbook 30.5, Callings in the Church (churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/30-callings-in-the-church).

docs.title: Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Committee Leadership — paired calling

  • Reports To: YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs; also sits on the Stake YSA Council.
  • Positions Needed: One

Purpose

The Sister Co-Chair shares full ownership of the athletics calendar and program quality, with a particular focus on ensuring that every league, open-play night, and tournament is designed so everyone — sisters, newcomers, less-active YSAs, and non-members — feels genuinely included and welcome, in line with the Gathering Plan's "belonging matters more than headcount" standard.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-chairs the committee with the Priesthood Co-Chair, sharing full ownership of the calendar and program quality.
  • Makes sure every league, open-play night, and tournament is designed so everyone feels included, welcome, and belongs.
  • Works with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads to make sure less-active and new-move-in YSAs get personally invited.
  • Coordinates recruiting and training Connection Hosts with the Ward Athletics Representatives.
  • Tracks weekly attendance, absentee follow-up, and less-active/non-member turnout alongside the Priesthood Co-Chair.

Implementation Ideas

  • Build a simple "everyone belongs" pre-night checklist — greeters staffed, teams mixed across wards, a newcomer follow-up owner assigned — and run it before every league or open-play night.
  • Keep one shared sheet tracking weekly attendance and 48-hour follow-up completion side by side with the Priesthood Co-Chair so nothing slips.
  • Meet monthly with the Gathering Specialists / Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads to get specific names — not just numbers — of less-active or new-move-in YSAs to personally invite.
  • Train every new Connection Host with the same short checklist: greet, learn names, invite to what's next, hand off newcomer/absentee names within 48 hours.
  • Give a quick shout-out in Committee meetings when a newcomer returns a second time, reinforcing that belonging, not headcount, is the measure of success.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §4.2, §7.2; Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §1, §5; Part 2 §1 ("belonging matters more than headcount"); Boise YSA Stake Gathering Specialist role description ("Know Them by Name").

docs.title: Sport Commissioner
docs.text:
One per active sport, per season

  • Reports To: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs.
  • Positions Needed: Four to six (rotating by season)

Purpose

The Sport Commissioner oversees one sport — volleyball, basketball, futsal, softball, pickleball, flag football, or ultimate frisbee — for its season, translating the Gathering Plan's athletics vision into a real schedule, real teams, and a season that opens and closes on time.

Key Responsibilities

  • Owns scheduling, rules, equipment, and officiating for one sport during its season.
  • Recruits and briefs Team Captains for that sport, and makes sure teams are mixed across wards so people aren't just playing with the same ward crowd.
  • Works with the Facility & Equipment Steward on reservations and makes sure scheduling respects the Sabbath.
  • Runs the season opener and closer, including the stake tournament at the end.
  • Reports weekly attendance, any incidents, and roster changes to the Committee Secretary.

Implementation Ideas

  • Put together a one-page season packet for each sport — schedule, roster rules, officiating plan, safety basics — and hand it to every Team Captain at recruitment.
  • Shadow the outgoing Commissioner for a full season before taking over solo, whenever the calendar allows.
  • Keep a running handoff document (facility contacts, equipment inventory, open items, lessons learned) updated continuously, not just at the end of the season.
  • Mix rosters across wards at sign-up, before the season starts, so cross-ward friendships form from week one.
  • Report weekly attendance and incidents to the Committee Secretary on the same simple form every week so nothing depends on memory.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §4.3, §5, §11; Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §2B.

docs.title: Team Captain
docs.text:
One per team, per season

  • Reports To: Sport Commissioner (functionally).
  • Positions Needed: Eight to twelve (rotating by season)

Purpose

A Team Captain looks out for teammates, not just plays with them — the on-the-court version of shepherding that keeps every player known, contacted, and welcomed, favoring YSAs who haven't led before so the calling helps them grow.

Key Responsibilities

  • Looks out for teammates, not just plays with them: knows everyone's name, tracks attendance, and reaches out to anyone who misses within 48 hours.
  • Welcomes non-members, investigators, and less-active YSAs onto the team, no exceptions.
  • Pairs up active YSAs with less-active or new teammates ("Adopt a Player").
  • Leads a short prayer and a spiritual thought when a Commissioner or Connection Host isn't present.
  • Reports attendance and follow-up needs to the Sport Commissioner after each game.

Implementation Ideas

  • Keep a simple roster sheet with name, ward, and a "contacted this week" checkbox — a lightweight version of the ward's monthly contact tracker.
  • Set a personal 48-hour rule: anyone who misses a game gets a text or call before the next one, mirroring the stake-wide absentee standard.
  • Run "Adopt a Player" proactively — pair a new or less-active teammate with an active one before the first game, not after someone starts slipping away.
  • Prepare a short prayer or spiritual thought ahead of time for weeks the Commissioner or Connection Host can't attend, and rotate who gives it.
  • Report attendance and follow-up needs to the Sport Commissioner right after each game, while it's still fresh.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §4.4, §5; Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §2B, §5 ("Adopt a Player"); General Handbook 30, Callings in the Church (new members grow through service).

docs.title: Connection Host (Athletics)
docs.text:
Two per night, rotating

  • Reports To: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs (functionally); on-site Sport Commissioner.
  • Positions Needed: Two per night (rotating)

Purpose

A Connection Host is a called greeter whose entire job is to find whoever's standing alone at an open-play, league, or tournament night, learn their name, and make sure they're followed up with — often the easiest calling for someone building confidence on a first assignment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Greets people at every open-play, league, and tournament night, finds whoever's standing alone, and learns their name.
  • Encourages people to bring a friend, and welcomes newcomers, investigators, and less-active YSAs.
  • Leads the pre-game prayer and spiritual thought when no Commissioner is around.
  • Passes the names of newcomers and absentees to the appropriate Team Captain or Sport Commissioner for follow-up within 48 hours.

Implementation Ideas

  • Arrive early enough to greet people at the door rather than starting once play begins, so no one arrives without a welcome.
  • Keep a small notecard or phone note during the night to jot newcomer and absentee names on the spot for hand-off within 48 hours.
  • Personally invite one newcomer or guest to "bring a friend" to the next event, every single night.
  • Rotate leading the pre-game prayer and spiritual thought when no Commissioner is present, building comfort with a first calling.
  • Debrief for two minutes with the Sport Commissioner after each night: who was new, who seemed to be standing alone, who needs a follow-up call.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §4.5, §5; Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §2A ("bring a friend"); General Handbook 4.2, Leadership and Councils in the Church of Jesus Christ.

docs.title: Facility & Equipment Steward
docs.text:
Stays in place year-round

  • Reports To: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs.
  • Positions Needed: One (12–18 month term)

Purpose

The Facility & Equipment Steward keeps the physical side of athletics running — handling building access, reservations, gear, and safety — so Sabbath conflicts, missing equipment, and unresolved safety issues never derail a season.

Key Responsibilities

  • Handles building access, court and field reservations, and keeps scheduling Sabbath-respectful across wards.
  • Keeps the shared equipment inventory up to date, and hands out and collects gear each season.
  • Owns first aid kits, injury procedures, concussion awareness, and any liability/release forms.
  • Brings unresolved facility conflicts to the Priesthood Co-Chair to sort out with bishops.

Implementation Ideas

  • Maintain one master booking calendar covering every gym and field reservation across wards, checked weekly against the season calendar for Sabbath conflicts.
  • Keep a simple equipment checklist — in/out, condition, season assigned — updated every time gear changes hands.
  • Stock and check first aid kits before each season begins, and post a written injury/incident procedure where Commissioners can find it fast.
  • Route liability or release forms through the office in advance of any tournament or off-site inter-stake event, per General Handbook activity-approval guidelines.
  • Escalate any facility conflict to the Priesthood Co-Chair the same week it appears, rather than letting it sit until game day.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §4.6, §9; Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §6; General Handbook 20.7, Safety Policies and Guidelines for Activities (churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/20-activities).

docs.title: Ward Athletics Representatives (Rep A & Rep B)
docs.text:
Ward-Level — two per ward (Rep A: Elders Quorum Counselor · Rep B: Relief Society Counselor)

  • Reports To: Athletics Co-Chairs (day-to-day); ward bishopric liaison (for pastoral matters).
  • Positions Needed: Two per ward — Rep A (Counselor, Ward Elders Quorum Presidency) and Rep B (Counselor, Ward Relief Society Presidency)

Purpose

The Ward Athletics Representatives bring the Athletics Committee's work home to a specific ward, organized by organization so both brothers and sisters receive personal attention. Rep A works from the Elders Quorum and Rep B from the Relief Society, each personally inviting people in their respective organizations, tracking their organizations' attendance, and following up with newcomers and no-shows within 48 hours — the personal, one-by-one outreach that keeps activities from becoming impersonal calendar postings.

Key Responsibilities

  • These are the ward's existing Ward Representatives (§4.14 of the Stake YSA Council Charter) — the Counselor in the Ward Elders Quorum Presidency (Representative A) and the Counselor in the Ward Relief Society Presidency (Representative B) — no separate calling needed.
  • Each promotes athletics within their respective organization and personally invites people to open play, leagues, and tournaments.
  • Tracks the ward's athletics attendance alongside activities and enrichment for their organization, and follows up with that organization's newcomers and absentees within 48 hours.
  • Attends the monthly Stake YSA Council meeting and flags any facility, safety, or participation concerns to the Athletics Co-Chairs.

Implementation Ideas

  • Pull your organization's YSA roster monthly (Elders Quorum for Representative A, Relief Society for Representative B) and check it against athletics attendance, flagging anyone who hasn't shown up in 30-plus days.
  • Send a personal invite — not just an announcement — to each YSA in your organization before every open-play night and league season kicks off.
  • Coordinate with your counterpart Representative before each season so invitations and follow-up cover the whole ward without duplicating effort or leaving gaps.
  • Follow up with newcomers and absentees from your organization's athletics participation within 48 hours, using the same rhythm as your other Ward Representative assignments.
  • Bring specific names and situations, not just numbers, to the monthly Stake YSA Council meeting, and carry stake-level athletics assignments back to your ward council.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §3.3, §4.7; Stake YSA Council Charter §4.14 (Ward Representatives); Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §4; Boise YSA Stake Gathering Specialist role description ("Know Them by Name," roster reconciliation).

docs.title: Married Couple Advisors
docs.text:
Mentors, not managers — assigned by the stake presidency

  • Reports To: Athletics Committee Co-Chairs (as mentors, not managers).
  • Positions Needed: Assigned by the stake presidency, as needed

Purpose

Following the Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise YSA Stake, married couples serve as mentors and role models rather than managers — showing up, encouraging, and sharing their experience without planning, running, or refereeing in place of a YSA leader.

Key Responsibilities

  • Show up to open-play nights, league games, and tournaments as guests and friends, not running things per the stake's married-couple guidance.
  • Offer experience and encouragement to Sport Commissioners and Team Captains when asked or prompted. Never plan, run, or referee in place of a YSA leader.
  • Model "connection before competition" and the adult-to-adult boundaries laid out in A Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise Idaho YSA Stake.
  • Coordinate who attends when with the Priesthood Co-Chair.

Implementation Ideas

  • Show up consistently to the same sport or season so YSAs get to know the couple by name.
  • Offer feedback or encouragement only when a Commissioner or Captain asks — resist the instinct to referee, coach, or run things.
  • Coordinate attendance plans with the Priesthood Co-Chair each season so coverage is spread across nights rather than concentrated on a few.
  • Share brief personal experiences or encouragement with Commissioners and Captains one-on-one after games, modeling "connection before competition."
  • Review A Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise YSA Stake before each new season as a refresher.

Reference

  • Athletics Committee Charter and Meeting Plan §3.4, §4.8, §10, §11; Comprehensive Gathering Plan, Part 3 §1.

docs.title: Charter and Meeting Plan Summary
docs.text: Stake Education and Enrichment Committee — Charter and Meeting Plan — One Page Summary

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: This charter establishes the Education & Enrichment Committee, which delivers Part 4 of the Gathering Plan and staffs the two Co-Chair seats named in the YSA Council Charter. It defines the Committee's structure, roles, meeting rhythm, and reporting line so the Stake YSA Council can steer the vision while the Committee owns day-to-day execution.

docs.title: Committee Structure
docs.text:
A fixed, ten-member Committee Core (all Young Single Adults), supported by advisor couples and a seasonal Facilitator & Mentor Network:

Layer Composition Size Committee (Tier 1) Co-Chairs + 8 coordinators, all YSAs 10 members Advisor Couples Married couples per the Guide for Married Couples; non-voting 2–3 couples Facilitator & Mentor Network (Tier 2) Facilitators, presenters, hosts, mentors recruited each curriculum cycle 15–25, seasonal

Ten seats: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (Sister & Priesthood-YSA High Councilor), Monthly Enrichment Night Producer, Small-Group Facilitator Coordinator, Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator, Discussion Group Coordinator, Mentorship Pairing Coordinator, Institute & Covenant Progression Liaison, Learning & Enrichment Coordinator, and Committee Secretary/Metrics Recorder. Young single adults plan, run, and teach every session; advisor couples support and mentor without leading.

New — Learning & Enrichment Coordinator: the Committee's needs-and-resources hub. Gathers members' interests, talents, and needs; keeps a stake-wide resource list of teachers, presenters, and experts; recommends 3–5 Christ-centered topics each cycle; and plans firesides and pilot workshops. Supplies topics, speakers, facilitators, mentors, and needs data to the other Coordinators and the Secretary, and hands proven pilots to the Workshop & Seminar Coordinator so the two seats never compete.

docs.title: Meeting & Reporting
docs.text: Meeting Frequency Purpose Committee Core Meeting Biweekly (first 90 days), then monthly Review curriculum calendar and needs summary; coordinate facilitators, workshops, mentors Needs & Resources Huddle Monthly, before Committee meeting Learning & Enrichment, Workshop, and Producer match needs to topics and presenters Enrichment Night Debrief Monthly Assess belonging, attendance, and the commitment invitation YSA Council Report Monthly Co-Chairs deliver the stewardship report, incl. member needs, to the Executive Co-Chairs Quarterly Curriculum Review Quarterly Progress check on the four curriculum threads and the quarter's needs patterns

docs.title: Decision Rights
docs.text:
• Committee decides on its own: enrichment-night/workshop content and calendar; facilitator, presenter, and mentor recruitment and assignment; needs-driven workshops and firesides within the approved budget and calendar.
  • Committee recommends, Executive Co-Chairs approve: coordinator or advisor-couple changes; any paid presenter, honorarium, or spending beyond the enrichment budget; content and distribution of a stake-wide member interest survey.
  • Escalates immediately: building-use conflicts (Executive Co-Chairs resolve) and sensitive individual situations (go straight to bishops or stake presidency). Survey responses are reported as patterns, never names.

docs.title: First 90 Days
docs.text: Weeks 1–2: confirm charter and Advisor assignments. Weeks 2–4: call Coordinators/Secretary; recruit first facilitators; Learning & Enrichment Coordinator sets scope with the Priesthood Co-Chair. Weeks 4–6: first Committee Core meeting and Enrichment Night scheduled; leader needs gathering begins and survey submitted for approval. Weeks 6–8: first Enrichment Night runs; workshop calendar published; first resource list shared. Weeks 8–12: first stewardship report delivered; discussion groups launch; first needs summary reported and pilot workshop or fireside planned.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A ten-member, YSA-led Committee with clear, undivided ownership of each Part 4 delivery format; a Learning & Enrichment Coordinator who grounds every offering in members' real interests, talents, and needs; a Facilitator & Mentor Network that carries the four curriculum threads into every small group; and a single reporting chain that keeps the Stake YSA Council informed and able to steer the vision.

docs.title: Stake Education & Enrichment Committee — Detailed Charter and Meeting Plan
docs.text:
Boise Idaho YSA Stake — Stake Education and Enrichment Committee — Charter and Meeting Plan

Companion document to the Boise Idaho YSA Stake Comprehensive Gathering Plan and the Stake YSA Council Charter and Meeting Plan.

docs.title: 1. Purpose of This Document
docs.text:
The Boise YSA Stake Comprehensive Gathering Plan outlines the vision for reaching and gathering Young Single Adults. The Stake YSA Council Charter and Meeting Plan establishes the twelve-seat Executive Committee that delivers on that vision, including the two Education & Enrichment Co-Lead seats described in Sections 4.8 and 4.9 of that charter. This document brings those two seats and Part 4 of the Gathering Plan ("Education and Enrichment Curriculum") into action by creating a standing committee with its own structure, staffing, meeting rhythm, and accountability for day-to-day work.

The Gathering Plan outlines what the four curriculum threads and delivery formats must accomplish, and the YSA Council Charter identifies who owns Education & Enrichment at the Executive Committee level. This document explains how that ownership plays out week to week: how many coordinators and facilitators we need, how the work is divided among them, how married couple advisors help without leading, and how the Committee keeps the Stake YSA Executive Council in the loop through the Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs.

This document is meant to be adopted by the Stake YSA Executive Co-Chairs and used directly by the Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs as their working charter and onboarding guide for every coordinator, facilitator, mentor, and married-couple advisor on the Committee.

docs.title: 2. Relationship to the Gathering Plan and the YSA Council
docs.text:
The YSA Council Charter draws a clear line between the YSA Council, which owns outcomes across all four priorities, and the specialist committees under it, which own the execution of one piece of the plan. This charter keeps that same line for Education & Enrichment:

Body Role Stake YSA Council (Executive Co-Chairs) Extends or recommends the Education & Enrichment Co-Chair assignments and signs off on changes to Committee makeup. Sets the yearly budget for enrichment nights, workshops, and materials, and approves any spending outside that budget. Gets the Committee's monthly report and gives direction, counsel, and correction. Resolves building-use conflicts and other issues the Committee can't settle on its own. Education & Enrichment Committee Fully owns delivering Priority 2 ("Teach Divine Identity, Purpose, and Potential") and the enrichment-related parts of Priorities 3 and 4, through the Monthly Stake Enrichment Night, workshops, discussion groups, and mentorship pairings. Builds and runs the curriculum calendar across the four threads, recruits and trains facilitators and mentors, and tracks attendance, facilitator counts, and covenant-progression indicators. Works with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead so institute topics and stake enrichment topics reinforce each other. Gathers members' interests, talents, and needs and keeps a stake-wide resource list of teachers, presenters, and subject-matter experts, so every offering responds to real member needs. Reports progress, risks, and needs to the Stake YSA Council on a set schedule (Section 6).

What the Committee can decide and run on its own, without asking first:

  • Content and scheduling for enrichment nights, workshops, discussion groups, and mentorship pairings within the four curriculum threads.
  • Recruiting, training, and assigning facilitators, presenters, and mentors.
  • Forming, rotating, or changing the format of small groups to help people feel like they belong.
  • Gathering member needs from ward and stake leaders, keeping the stake resource list, and planning needs-driven workshops and firesides within the approved budget and curriculum calendar.

What needs to go to the Stake YSA Executive Co-Chairs before moving forward:

  • Any new coordinator calling, release, or change to who's on the Committee.
  • A new paid presenter, honorarium, or any spending beyond the approved enrichment budget.
  • The scope and wording of any stake-wide member interest survey before it is distributed.
  • Building scheduling conflicts with priesthood or other stake and ward activities.
  • Sensitive situations that come up through mentorship or small groups — mental health crises, worthiness concerns, safety issues — these go straight to the bishops or stake presidency, not handled inside the Committee.

docs.title: 3. Committee Structure and Composition
docs.text: The Committee works in two tiers, matching the two-tier design used across the YSA Council: a Committee Core that owns outcomes and reports to the Executive Co-Chairs, and a Facilitator & Mentor Network that carries the curriculum into every small group, workshop, and mentoring relationship.

docs.title: 3.1 Tier 1 — Committee
docs.text:
Ten seats, all filled by Young Single Adults, each one owning a clearly defined piece of Education and Enrichment. Use these seat names exactly when calling or briefing Committee members.

Seat Name Owns Advisor Couple(s) Education & Enrichment Co-Chair (Sister) TBD (Sister) Co-Chairs the Committee; leads sister-facing facilitator and mentor recruiting; designs small groups so everyone feels they belong. Education & Enrichment Co-Chair (Priesthood) High Councilor Co-chairs the Committee; keeps the curriculum aligned with the Institute; ensures teaching standards are followed. Monthly Enrichment Night Producer Runs the Monthly Stake Enrichment Night — worship, the teaching slot, small-group logistics, and the closing invitation to commit. Small-Group Facilitator Coordinator Recruits, trains, and schedules cross-ward small-group facilitators for every enrichment night. Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator Runs the quarterly workshop calendar (career, financial literacy, wellness, scripture study, marriage prep, parenting) and recruits presenters. Discussion Group Coordinator Runs small, recurring book and article discussion groups centered on Christ, identity, and purpose. Mentorship Pairing Coordinator Pairs YSAs with mature stake members for life, career, and spiritual guidance; maintains a monthly mentor-meeting cadence. Institute & Covenant Progression Liaison Works with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead and institute faculty so course topics line up with the four threads. Learning & Enrichment Coordinator Gathers member interests, talents, and needs; keeps the stake resource list; plans needs-based workshops and firesides. Committee Secretary / Metrics Recorder Keeps minutes, attendance, and facilitator data, and puts together the monthly enrichment stewardship report.

Committee Core total: 10 members.

docs.title: 3.2 Tier 2 — Facilitator and Mentor Network
docs.text: In line with the Gathering Plan's delivery formats, the Committee recruits small-group facilitators for the Monthly Enrichment Night, presenters for the Workshop & Seminar Series, hosts for Discussion Groups, and mentors for the Mentorship Pairing program every curriculum cycle. Network members aren't standing Committee members; they're trained and assigned by the relevant Coordinator, show up for the sessions they're assigned to, and report attendance and participation to that Coordinator after every session. When recruiting, Coordinators start with the stake resource list kept by the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator.

docs.title: 3.3 Married Couple Advisors
docs.text: Per A Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise YSA Stake, married couples called to this committee serve as advisors, not leaders. They sit with the Co-Chairs during Committee planning, are available as mentors in the Mentorship Pairing pool, and may be invited by the Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator to speak on marriage prep, parenting, or career and financial topics based on their own experience. With their permission, their skills and teaching interests are added to the stake resource list. Young single adults plan, run, and teach every enrichment night, workshop, and discussion group; advisor couples support and attend.

docs.title: 3.4 Suggested Total Committee Size
docs.text:
Layer Composition Size Committee (Tier 1) Co-Chairs and eight coordinators, all Young Single Adults 10 members Standing Advisor Couples Married couples serving per the Guide for Married Couples; non-voting 2–3 couples Facilitator & Mentor Network (Tier 2) Small-group facilitators, workshop presenters, discussion-group hosts, and mentors, recruited each curriculum cycle 15–25, seasonal

Keep the Committee fixed at ten; that keeps accountability clear and undivided for each delivery format in Part 4 of the Gathering Plan and for the needs-and-resources work that feeds them, while letting the Facilitator & Mentor Network grow and shrink with the season and curriculum cycle.

docs.title: 4. Roles, Responsibilities, and Assignments
docs.text: Each Committee seat below is written as a standing assignment description, matching the format used in Section 4 of the YSA Council Charter. Use these descriptions as-is when calling or briefing Committee members.

docs.title: 4.1 Education & Enrichment Committee Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Reports to: YSA Council Co-Chairs (jointly with Priesthood Co-Chair)

  • Co-leads the Education & Enrichment Committee; co-chairs every Committee Core meeting with the Priesthood Executive Co-Chair.
  • Runs the Monthly Stake Enrichment Night and rotates through the four curriculum threads over the year, together with the Priesthood Co-Chair.
  • Champions sister-specific facilitator and mentor recruiting, and makes sure small groups are set up so no one sits alone.
  • Represents the Committee at the monthly YSA Council meeting alongside the Priesthood Co-Chair.
  • Makes sure every enrichment night ends with a specific invitation to take a covenant step.
  • Uses the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's needs summary when setting each enrichment night's emphasis and designing small groups.

Success metric: Monthly enrichment attendance and trend; facilitators trained per cycle.

docs.title: 4.2 Education & Enrichment Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Reports to: YSA Council Co-Chairs (jointly with Sister Co-Chair)

  • Co-leads the Education & Enrichment Committee; carries the Committee's reporting relationship with the YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs.
  • Coordinates the Workshop/Seminar series and keeps it aligned with the Institute, drawing on stake members' expertise.
  • Reviews Committee coordinator changes and recommends them to the YSA Council Co-Chairs.
  • Makes sure Christ-centered framing and doctrine-first teaching standards are upheld across every enrichment night, workshop, and discussion group.
  • Delivers the monthly enrichment stewardship report to the YSA Council Co-Chairs, prepared by the Secretary.
  • Serves as the assigned high councilor for the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator; reviews member-survey content and needs-based topic recommendations for Christ-centered framing and carries any that need approval to the Executive Co-Chairs.

Success metric: On-time monthly reports; teaching-standards compliance across all sessions.

docs.title: 4.3 Monthly Enrichment Night Producer
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs

  • Books the teaching slot and speaker for each month's enrichment night, matching the current curriculum thread.
  • Runs the standard format: brief worship (hymn, prayer), 35–40 minutes of teaching, small-group discussion, and a personal commitment invitation.
  • Coordinates room setup and logistics with the building scheduler and the Communications & Calendar Lead.
  • Makes sure the night is on the master calendar at least 60 days ahead of time.
  • Runs a quick post-event debrief with the Small-Group Facilitator Coordinator and reports attendance to the Secretary.
  • Draws on the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's topic recommendations and resource list when booking speakers, and shares commitment-invitation patterns that point to new needs.

Success metric: On-time, quality-bar enrichment night delivered monthly; commitment-invitation completion noted.

docs.title: 4.4 Small-Group Facilitator Coordinator
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs

  • Recruits and trains 6–10-person cross-ward small-group facilitators for every enrichment night.
  • Briefs facilitators on the teaching standards in Section 6 of Part 4 of the Gathering Plan: doctrine first, Christ-centered, interactive, safe space, confidentiality, and referral pathways.
  • Assigns facilitators to groups each cycle, and makes sure no facilitator stays with the same group long enough to form a clique.
  • Runs a short debrief after each enrichment night and passes facilitator counts and notes to the Secretary.
  • Recruits potential facilitators from the stake resource list, and passes recurring debrief themes (without names) to the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator for the needs summary.

Success metric: Facilitators trained per cycle; small-group belonging feedback.

docs.title: 4.5 Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs

  • Builds the quarterly workshop calendar: career development, financial literacy, mental and emotional wellness, scripture study and prayer methods, marriage prep and healthy dating, and parenting basics.
  • Recruits presenters from among stake members with relevant expertise, starting with the stake resource list, including married-couple advisors where appropriate.
  • Coordinates logistics and makes sure every workshop is framed around divine identity, purpose, or potential rather than feeling like a stand-alone class.
  • Reports attendance and presenter-recruiting status to the Secretary each month.
  • Builds the quarterly calendar from the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's needs summary, meets with that Coordinator in the monthly Needs & Resources Huddle (Section 6), and takes on pilot topics that prove useful as recurring workshops.

Success metric: Workshops delivered per quarter; attendance and presenter pipeline health.

docs.title: 4.6 Discussion Group Coordinator
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs

  • Forms small, recurring 4–8-person discussion groups studying Come, Follow Me, recent general conference talks, or approved Church resources.
  • Recruits and briefs group hosts on confidentiality and the fundamentals of leading a discussion.
  • Tracks group health, attendance, retention, and whether groups are building real depth and connection, not just showing up.
  • Reports the number of active groups and the participation trend to the Secretary.
  • Uses member-interest survey results from the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator to choose study topics and to invite new participants and hosts.

Success metric: Number of active discussion groups; average attendance and retention.

docs.title: 4.7 Mentorship Pairing Coordinator
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs

  • Recruits mature stake members, including couples and individuals, such as married couple advisors, to serve as mentors for life, career, and spiritual guidance.
  • Pairs YSAs with mentors, paying particular attention to single YSAs who don't have family nearby.
  • Sets up a monthly mentor-meeting rhythm built around the four curriculum threads.
  • Tracks how the pairings are going and reports active-pairing counts and meeting completion to the Secretary.
  • Draws on the professional skills and life experience recorded on the stake resource list to build the mentor pool, and receives career, education, and life-transition needs flagged by the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator.

Success metric: Number of active mentor pairings; monthly meeting completion rate.

docs.title: 4.8 Institute & Covenant Progression Liaison
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (works with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead)

  • Partners with institute faculty and the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead to boost enrollment and clear away barriers like rides and scheduling.
  • Lines up institute course topics with the stake's four curriculum threads wherever possible.
  • Sends institute enrollment numbers relevant to Education & Enrichment programming to the Secretary each month.
  • Shares institute course offerings with the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator and uses needs patterns to recommend courses that complement, rather than duplicate, stake workshops and firesides.

Success metric: Institute enrollment rate among tracked YSAs; topic alignment with the annual curriculum arc.

docs.title: 4.9 Learning & Enrichment Coordinator
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (a stake calling serving under the direction of the stake presidency and the assigned high councilor, the Priesthood Co-Chair)

This seat is the Committee's needs-and-resources hub. It is more than event planning. It is a way of ministering: gathering members' interests, talents, and needs and connecting members with the people and resources that can bless them. Every offering it supports should help members feel seen, strengthen faith, and support covenant keeping.

Needs Gathering & Resource Coordination

  • Identifies member interests, talents, professional skills, and unmet needs through a short member interest survey, interviews, and leader input, with a focus on practical needs, spiritual interests, and life-transition challenges.
  • Gathers current needs each planning cycle from bishoprics, Relief Society and Elders Quorum presidencies, ward YSA leaders, and ministering interviews, asking each leader, "What are the most common needs or gaps you see among our YSA members?" and combines the answers with survey results.
  • Keeps the stake-wide resource list of willing teachers, presenters, and subject-matter experts (topic, audience, suggested presenter, cost, location, and spiritual purpose), reviews it each planning cycle, and shares it with every Coordinator.
  • Matches needs with available resources so offerings are useful, simple, and reasonably cost-effective.

Workshop & Fireside Planning

  • Recommends 3 to 5 topics each planning cycle that fit stake priorities and the current curriculum thread, each paired with a Christ-centered framing so practical help points members toward deeper faith and covenant living.
  • Plans and coordinates stake firesides and needs-driven practical classes, starting with one pilot (for example, a "Faith and Future" workshop with a short devotional, a practical class, and a testimony-bearing close), and helps with promotion and follow-up.
  • Hands pilot topics that prove useful to the Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator for the quarterly calendar, so the two seats never run competing events.
  • Gathers feedback after each event and reports needs patterns, attendance, feedback, and recommended future topics to the Secretary and the Co-Chairs.

Success metric: Members surveyed or interviewed; top recurring needs identified; resources added to the list; workshops and firesides held and their attendance; share of Committee topics traced to identified needs.

How This Seat Coordinates with the Committee

Committee Member How the Work Is Coordinated Co-Chairs Meets with the Co-Chairs at the start of the term to set scope, the survey approval process, and reporting expectations. Delivers a needs-and-topics summary each planning cycle. The Priesthood Co-Chair reviews framing and carries survey content and spending requests to the Executive Co-Chairs. Monthly Enrichment Night Producer Supplies needs-based topic ideas and possible speakers from the resource list for each curriculum thread; gets back attendance and commitment-invitation patterns that reveal new needs. Small-Group Facilitator Coordinator Shares members with teaching or facilitation talents as possible facilitators; gets back recurring debrief themes, without names, for the needs summary. Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator Closest partner. The Learning & Enrichment Coordinator owns needs gathering, topic recommendations, firesides, and pilots; the Workshop Coordinator owns the quarterly calendar and presenter scheduling. They meet monthly in the Needs & Resources Huddle to align calendars, avoid duplicate topics, and hand off proven pilots and presenters. Discussion Group Coordinator Passes along survey interest in specific books, talks, or gospel topics, plus names of members who want to join or host a group. Mentorship Pairing Coordinator Shares professional skills and life experience from the resource list to grow the mentor pool; flags career, education, and life-transition needs that a mentor can meet better than a class. Institute & Covenant Progression Liaison Shares needs patterns so institute course recommendations and stake offerings complement each other; coordinates temple-preparation and covenant-focused topics with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead. Committee Secretary / Metrics Recorder Provides monthly needs-gathering and event metrics for the dashboard; the Secretary records the topic pipeline and related action items in the minutes. Married Couple Advisors Invites advisor couples to share skills for the resource list and to suggest topics from their experience; they counsel and support while young single adults plan and teach. Facilitator & Mentor Network Network members raise individual needs with their own Coordinator, who passes along patterns without names. Sensitive individual situations go to bishops and are never recorded on the needs list.

docs.title: 4.10 Committee Secretary / Metrics Recorder
docs.text:
Reports to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs

  • Takes minutes and tracks action items for every Committee Core meeting.
  • Pulls together the monthly attendance, facilitator, workshop, discussion-group, mentorship, and needs-gathering dashboard from data each Coordinator provides.
  • Drafts the monthly enrichment stewardship report for the Co-Chairs to deliver to the Executive Co-Chairs (Section 6.2).
  • Keeps track of the Committee roster, term dates, and any upcoming turnover or succession needs.

Success metric: Reports delivered on schedule; dashboard accuracy and completeness.

docs.title: 4.11 Married Couple Advisors
docs.text:
Advisory relationship to: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (not a supervisory reporting line)

  • Sit with the Committee Core in planning meetings as counsel, not as chairs; share experience when asked or when the Spirit prompts, never as a directive to follow.
  • Serve in the Mentorship Pairing pool as mentors, and may be invited to speak in the Workshop & Seminar Series on marriage, parenting, or career and financial topics; share their skills for the stake resource list and suggest topics when the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator asks.
  • Attend enrichment nights, workshops, and discussion groups as guests and friends, there to be present, not to run the program; young adult facilitators greet, lead, and teach.
  • Coach and encourage Coordinators privately; if something needs correcting, do it specifically, kindly, and away from the group, per the Guide for Married Couples.

Success metric: Mentor-pairing satisfaction; Coordinators report feeling supported, not managed.

docs.title: 4.12 Facilitator and Mentor Network (Tier 2)
docs.text:
Reports to: the relevant Coordinator (Small-Group Facilitator, Workshop & Seminar, Discussion Group, or Mentorship Pairing)

  • Complete training on teaching standards and confidentiality within two weeks of being assigned.
  • Attend every session they're assigned to, and immediately report attendance and participation notes to the Coordinator afterward.
  • Bring any individual needs, concerns, or opportunities to the Coordinator rather than handling sensitive situations on one's own.

Success metric: Session coverage rate; timeliness of post-session reporting.

docs.title: 5. Selection, Calling, and Term of Service
docs.text:
Seat How Selected Term Co-Chairs Nominated by the Stake YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs with input from the stake presidency; extended as a calling, interviewed, and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered Coordinators & Secretary Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Executive Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment ("Stake Education & Enrichment Specialist — [Function]"); interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered Married Couple Advisors Called by the stake presidency per General Handbook chapter 30, following the orientation in the Guide for Married Couples; interviewed and set apart. Concurrent with assignment; no fixed rotation Facilitator & Mentor Network Recruited by the relevant Coordinator each curriculum cycle or season; an informal assignment, not a calling, unless the ward extends one separately. One curriculum cycle or season, renewable

Stagger terms so no more than half of the Committee Core turns over at once. Build in a 4–6-week overlap between an outgoing and incoming Coordinator for the handoff, since the YSA population naturally moves around a lot.

docs.text: Meeting Frequency Attendees Purpose Output Full Education & Enrichment Committee Meeting Biweekly (first 90 days), then monthly Co-Chairs, Coordinators, Secretary A spiritual thought and prayer for specific YSAs; review the curriculum-thread calendar and the Learning & Enrichment needs-and-topics summary; coordinate facilitators, workshops, and mentors. Minutes and action items; updated facilitator, workshop, and mentor assignments Needs & Resources Huddle Monthly, about one week before the Committee meeting (30 minutes) Learning & Enrichment Coordinator, Workshop & Seminar Coordinator, Enrichment Night Producer; other Coordinators as needed Review new needs data and the resource list; match topics to presenters; align workshops, firesides, and enrichment-night topics so nothing is duplicated. Updated topic pipeline and resource list; topic recommendations for the Committee meeting Enrichment Night Debrief Monthly, right after each Enrichment Night Producer, Facilitator Coordinator, facilitators Look at belonging, attendance, and how the commitment invitation landed.
