Year-two curriculum arc and calendar

docs.title: 6.1 Reporting Chain
docs.text:
Information and accountability flow in one consistent line, so nothing gets lost between a facilitator or mentor and the stake presidency:

  1. Facilitators, presenters, discussion-group hosts, and mentors report attendance and participation notes to their Coordinator after every session.
  2. Coordinators pull together their program data ahead of the Committee Core meeting, and the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator adds the needs-and-topics summary.
  3. The Secretary combines all the Coordinator reports into one dashboard and drafts the monthly enrichment stewardship report.
  4. Co-Chairs review it, add narrative and requests, deliver the report to the Stake YSA Council Co-Chairs, and represent Education & Enrichment at the YSA Council meeting.

docs.title: 6.2 Monthly Enrichment Stewardship Report Template
docs.text:
The Secretary drafts this report every month for the Co-Chairs to deliver to the YSA Co-Chairs. Keep it to one page, following the Gathering Plan's measurement framework (Part 4, Section 8):

  • Attendance & Participation — enrichment night, workshop, discussion group, and mentor-pairing attendance versus last month and versus the roster.
  • Facilitator & Mentor Health — how many were trained and are active this cycle, and what's needed for the next cycle.
  • Covenant Progression — the change in institute enrollment, how well commitment invitations were followed through, and self-reported understanding of divine identity, purpose, and potential.
  • Member Needs & Resources — members surveyed or interviewed, top recurring needs, resources added to the stake resource list, workshops and firesides held from identified needs, and recommended future topics.
  • Look-Ahead — what's on the enrichment calendar for the next 60 days and what support is needed.
  • Risks, Needs & Decisions Requested — anything that needs the YSA Council Co-Chairs' approval or a decision.

docs.title: 6.3 Annual Curriculum Arc Cadence
docs.text:
Committee planning follows the Gathering Plan's annual curriculum arc, so enrichment nights, workshops, and mentorship line up with whatever thread the rest of the stake is teaching that quarter:

Period Thread Committee Focus September–November T2 — Divine Purpose ("Why I Am Here") Launch the year's enrichment-night rotation; recruit and train the first cycle of facilitators and mentors; run the first member interest survey. December T4 — Christ and Covenants Christmas-season emphasis; coordinate with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead on temple-night tie-ins. January–February T1 — Divine Identity ("Who God Says I Am") New-year workshop push (financial literacy, wellness); mid-cycle facilitator refresh. March–April T4 — Christ and Covenants Easter-season emphasis; support for the temple recommend campaign; discussion groups on the Atonement. May–July T3 — Divine Potential ("Who I Am Becoming") Marriage and family prep classes; mentorship pairing emphasis; summer workshop series. August Capstone synthesis of all four threads Quarterly Curriculum Review and Annual Curriculum Arc Planning for year two, informed by the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's annual needs summary.

docs.title: 7. Decision Rights and Escalation
docs.text: Decision Committee Authority Executive Co-Chair Authority Enrichment-night topic, workshop content, and calendar within the four threads Decides Informed Facilitator, presenter, and mentor recruitment and assignment Decides Informed Needs-driven workshop or fireside within the approved budget and curriculum calendar Decides Informed New paid presenter, honorarium, or spending beyond the approved enrichment budget line Recommends Approves Content and distribution of a stake-wide member interest survey Recommends Approves Extending or releasing Coordinator callings Recommends Approves and sets apart Extending or releasing Married Couple Advisors Recommends Approves; stake presidency sets apart Building-use or priesthood scheduling conflicts Coordinates Resolves conflicts Sensitive individual or pastoral situations surfaced through mentorship or small groups Flags immediately Handles with bishops

docs.title: 8. Committee Operating Norms
docs.text:
• Every meeting opens and closes with prayer, and starts with a short spiritual reflection tied to one of the four curriculum threads.
  • Young single adults plan, run, and teach every enrichment night, workshop, and discussion group; Married Couple Advisors support and attend, consistent with the Guide for Married Couples.
  • Coordinators bring facilitator and mentor names, not just numbers, to every meeting; the Committee follows the Spirit to specific people, in line with the Gathering Plan's "on-ramp, not destination" standard.
  • Anything about specific individuals: mentoring concerns and sensitive needs are kept confidential outside the Committee and shared with bishops only on a need-to-know basis.
  • Member survey responses and the needs list are kept confidential and reported as patterns, not names; any individual need that surfaces goes to the member's bishop rather than onto the resource list.
  • Decisions are made by consensus among the present Co-Chairs and Coordinators; if something can't be resolved, it goes to the YSA Council Co-Chairs within a week rather than remaining unsettled.
  • Coordinators are expected to attend Committee Core meetings. If a Coordinator can't attend, a trained replacement should attend in their place.
  • Married Couple Advisors maintain the adult-to-adult boundaries outlined in the Guide for Married Couples: they don't hover over activities as if supervising youth, they correct privately and praise publicly, and they exercise good judgment in one-on-one mentoring settings.

docs.title: 9. Onboarding, Training, and Succession
docs.text:
• New Committee members get an onboarding packet: this charter, Part 4 of the Gathering Plan, the YSA Council Charter, the current dashboard, and (for advisor couples) the Guide for Married Couples.
  • New Coordinators shadow their predecessor for one full meeting cycle before taking over fully, whenever the term overlap allows for it.
  • Each Coordinator keeps a living handoff document (presenter and facilitator contacts, curriculum notes, open action items, lessons learned) updated all the time, not just at turnover.
  • The Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's handoff also includes the current stake resource list, survey tools and results, and the topic pipeline.
  • Married Couple Advisors complete the First 30 Days orientation described in the Guide for Married Couples and meet with the high councilor who supports the assignment.
  • Facilitators, presenters, and mentors receive training on teaching standards and confidentiality within two weeks of being assigned.

docs.title: 10. First 90 Days: Implementation Checklist
docs.text:
Timeframe Milestones Weeks 1–2 Co-Chairs confirm this charter with the YSA Council Co-Chairs; identify Coordinator candidates; confirm Married Couple Advisor assignments. Weeks 2–4 Coordinators and Secretary called and set apart; first cycle of small-group facilitators recruited; the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator meets with the Priesthood Co-Chair to set scope, the survey approval process, and reporting expectations. Weeks 4–6 First Committee Core meeting; reporting templates and dashboard set up; first Monthly Enrichment Night scheduled on the current curriculum thread; leader needs gathering begins and the member interest survey goes to the Executive Co-Chairs for approval. Weeks 6–8 The first Monthly Enrichment Night runs with trained facilitators; the quarterly workshop calendar is published; and recruitment for mentorship pairings begins; the first stake resource list is shared with all Coordinators. Weeks 8–12 First monthly enrichment stewardship report delivered to the Executive Co-Chairs; first discussion groups launched; first quarterly curriculum review scheduled; the first needs-and-topics summary is reported and a pilot workshop or fireside is planned.

This checklist mirrors Phase 1 and the start of Phase 2 of the Gathering Plan's Implementation Timeline (Part 1, Section 13), and the First 90 Days schedule of the YSA Council Charter (Section 10), so the Education & Enrichment Committee moves forward on the same clock as the rest of the YSA Council.

docs.title: 11. Summary
docs.text: This charter establishes a ten-member Education & Enrichment Committee Core for the Boise YSA Stake, fully owned and run by Young Single Adults and co-led by the Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs named in the YSA Council Charter. It outlines eight coordinator seats, each with clear, undivided accountability for one delivery format or support function in Part 4 of the Gathering Plan, including a Learning & Enrichment Coordinator who grounds every offering in members' real interests, talents, and needs; a Facilitator & Mentor Network that carries the four curriculum threads into every small group, workshop, and mentoring relationship; and a defined place for married couple advisors who train, coach, and support without leading. A steady meeting rhythm and a single reporting chain keep the Stake YSA Council informed and able to steer the vision and grant approvals. At the same time, the Committee has real ownership, clear accountability, and a direct line back to the plan's four priorities.

docs.title: Stake Education & Enrichment Committee — Roles
docs.text: Boise Idaho YSA Stake — Education & Enrichment Committee

docs.title: Education & Enrichment Committee Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Co-Chair

Section 4.1 of the Charter

  • Reports To: YSA Council Co-Chairs (jointly with the Priesthood Co-Chair)
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Stake YSA Council Co-Chairs with stake presidency input; called, interviewed, and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered with the Priesthood Co-Chair.

Purpose

The Sister Co-Chair co-chairs the Education & Enrichment Committee and shares full accountability for delivering Priority 2 ("Teach Divine Identity, Purpose, and Potential") through the Monthly Stake Enrichment Night, workshops, discussion groups, and mentorship pairings (Gathering Plan, Part 4). This role carries particular responsibility for sister-facing recruiting and for ensuring that every small group is a place where someone can belong.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-leads the Education & Enrichment Committee; co-chairs every Committee Core meeting with the Priesthood Executive Co-Chair.
  • Runs the Monthly Stake Enrichment Night and rotates through the four curriculum threads over the year, together with the Priesthood Co-Chair (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 4A).
  • Champions sister-specific facilitator and mentor recruiting, and makes sure small groups are set up so no one sits alone.
  • Represents the Committee at the monthly YSA Council meeting alongside the Priesthood Co-Chair.
  • Makes sure every enrichment night ends with a specific invitation to take a covenant step.
  • Uses the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's needs summary when setting each enrichment night's emphasis and designing small groups.

Implementation Ideas

  • Keep a running roster of trained sister facilitators and mentors, noting who is assigned each curriculum cycle.
  • Build a shared cross-ward seating chart with the Priesthood Co-Chair so newcomers are never grouped alone.
  • Write a short "greet and connect" script for hosts to use in the first five minutes of every enrichment night.
  • Track which sisters have been personally invited to serve each thread rotation, not just who volunteered.
  • Debrief after every enrichment night on whether the closing invitation was given and how it landed.

docs.title: Education & Enrichment Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Co-Chair

Section 4.2 of the Charter

  • Reports To: YSA Council Co-Chairs (jointly with the Sister Co-Chair)
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Stake YSA Council Co-Chairs with stake presidency input; called, interviewed, and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered with the Sister Co-Chair.

Purpose

The Priesthood Co-Chair co-chairs the Committee and maintains its formal reporting relationship with the YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs. This role keeps the Workshop & Seminar Series aligned with the Institute and upholds the doctrine-first, Christ-centered teaching standard across every enrichment night, workshop, and discussion group (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 6).

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-leads the Education & Enrichment Committee; carries the Committee's reporting relationship with the YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs.
  • Coordinates the Workshop/Seminar series and keeps it aligned with the Institute, drawing on stake members' expertise.
  • Reviews Committee coordinator changes and recommends them to the YSA Council Co-Chairs.
  • Makes sure Christ-centered framing and doctrine-first teaching standards are upheld across every enrichment night, workshop, and discussion group.
  • Delivers the monthly enrichment stewardship report to the YSA Council Co-Chairs, prepared by the Secretary.
  • Serves as the assigned high councilor for the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator; reviews member-survey content and needs-based topics for Christ-centered framing and carries approvals to the Executive Co-Chairs.

Implementation Ideas

  • Use a short "doctrine-first checklist" with every presenter or facilitator before they teach for the first time.
  • Sit in on one enrichment night, workshop, or discussion group each quarter to sample teaching quality firsthand.
  • Keep a one-page coordinator roster with term dates, flagged 60 days ahead of any turnover.
  • Use the Section 6.2 measurement framework as a fixed template so the monthly stewardship report is quick to assemble.
  • Compare Institute course topics against the current curriculum thread each term to catch alignment gaps early.

docs.title: Monthly Enrichment Night Producer
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.3 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

The Producer owns the delivery of the Monthly Stake Enrichment Night — the flagship format for Priority 2, rotating through the four curriculum threads throughout the year (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 4A). Success means a well-run night every month, with a clear next step offered at the end.

Key Responsibilities

  • Books the teaching slot and speaker for each month's enrichment night, matching the current curriculum thread.
  • Runs the standard format: brief worship (hymn, prayer), 35–40 minutes of teaching, small-group discussion, and a personal commitment invitation.
  • Coordinates room setup and logistics with the building scheduler and the Communications & Calendar Lead.
  • Makes sure the night is on the master calendar at least 60 days ahead of time.
  • Runs a quick post-event debrief with the Small-Group Facilitator Coordinator and reports attendance to the Secretary.
  • Draws on the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's topic recommendations and resource list when booking speakers, and shares commitment-invitation patterns that point to new needs.

Implementation Ideas

  • Build a 60-day production calendar: speaker booked → room reserved → topic confirmed → promotion sent → facilitators assigned.
  • Keep a rotating "speaker bench" of 8–10 approved teachers per curriculum thread so slots are never scrambled last minute.
  • Use a repeatable run-of-show template (opening hymn/prayer, teaching, small groups, commitment invite, closing) for every night.
  • Log which commitment invitation was given each month and roughly how many responded, for the debrief.
  • Confirm next month's thread and speaker before leaving each debrief meeting.

docs.title: Small-Group Facilitator Coordinator
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.4 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

This Coordinator builds and trains the Facilitator & Mentor Network members who lead cross-ward small-group discussions at every enrichment night — the setting where real belonging happens (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 4A). Training covers the six teaching standards: doctrine first, Christ-centered, interactive, safe space, confidentiality, and referral pathways.

Key Responsibilities

  • Recruits and trains 6–10-person cross-ward small-group facilitators for every enrichment night.
  • Briefs facilitators on the teaching standards in Section 6 of Part 4 of the Gathering Plan: doctrine first, Christ-centered, interactive, safe space, confidentiality, and referral pathways.
  • Assigns facilitators to groups each cycle, and makes sure no facilitator stays with the same group long enough to form a clique.
  • Runs a short debrief after each enrichment night and passes facilitator counts and notes to the Secretary.
  • Recruits potential facilitators from the stake resource list, and passes recurring debrief themes (without names) to the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator.

Implementation Ideas

  • Maintain a facilitator roster with training-completion dates and current assignment.
  • Hand every new facilitator a one-page card covering the six teaching standards at training.
  • Rotate facilitator-to-group assignments each cycle with a simple numbered draw so no one defaults to the same group.
  • Build a "when to refer" card pointing facilitators to the bishop for worthiness, safety, or mental-health concerns.
  • Send a two-question post-night survey to facilitators (what went well / who needs follow-up) and log it for the Secretary.

docs.title: Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.5 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

This Coordinator develops the quarterly workshop calendar covering career, financial literacy, wellness, scripture study, marriage prep, and parenting — practical topics aligned with divine identity, purpose, and potential (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 4C). The intended audience for every session is young single adults ages 18–35.

Key Responsibilities

  • Builds the quarterly workshop calendar: career development, financial literacy, mental and emotional wellness, scripture study and prayer methods, marriage prep and healthy dating, and parenting basics.
  • Recruits presenters from among stake members with relevant expertise, starting with the stake resource list, including married-couple advisors where appropriate.
  • Coordinates logistics and makes sure every workshop is framed around divine identity, purpose, or potential rather than feeling like a stand-alone class.
  • Reports attendance and presenter-recruiting status to the Secretary each month.
  • Builds the quarterly calendar from the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator's needs summary, meets monthly in the Needs & Resources Huddle, and takes on pilot topics that prove useful.

Implementation Ideas

  • Keep a presenter pipeline sheet: topic, presenter, confirmed date, and a backup presenter.
  • Ask every presenter to open with a one-minute tie-back to divine identity, purpose, or potential before the content begins.
  • Publish the quarterly calendar one quarter ahead so presenters get at least 8 weeks of lead time.
  • Invite married-couple advisors specifically for marriage-prep, parenting, and financial sessions, consistent with their advisory role.
  • Log a short presenter-quality note after each workshop so strong presenters get repeat invitations.

docs.title: Discussion Group Coordinator
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.6 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

This Coordinator runs small, recurring discussion groups (4–8 people) centered on Come, Follow Me, general conference talks, and other approved Church resources — a format that offers depth a large event can't (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 4D).

Key Responsibilities

  • Forms small, recurring 4–8-person discussion groups studying Come, Follow Me, recent general conference talks, or approved Church resources.
  • Recruits and briefs group hosts on confidentiality and the fundamentals of leading a discussion.
  • Tracks group health, attendance, retention, and whether groups are building real depth and connection, not just showing up.
  • Reports the number of active groups and the participation trend to the Secretary.
  • Uses member-interest survey results from the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator to choose study topics and invite new participants and hosts.

Implementation Ideas

  • Keep a directory of active groups with host name, meeting night, and location.
  • Give every new host a one-page "hosting basics" card: open with prayer, ask open questions, watch for the quiet person, close with a takeaway.
  • Check in with each host quarterly on group health, not just attendance numbers.
  • Refresh a group that has been static with the same 4–5 people for more than two cycles, to keep belonging fresh.
  • Keep a standing list of approved discussion resources so hosts never scramble for material.

docs.title: Mentorship Pairing Coordinator
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.7 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

This Coordinator pairs young single adults with mature stake members for life, career, and spiritual guidance — especially valuable for YSAs without nearby family (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 4E). Because mentoring conversations are personal, confidentiality and clear referral pathways matter more here than in any other seat.

Key Responsibilities

  • Recruits mature stake members, including couples and individuals, such as married couple advisors, to serve as mentors for life, career, and spiritual guidance.
  • Pairs YSAs with mentors, paying particular attention to single YSAs who don't have family nearby.
  • Sets up a monthly mentor-meeting rhythm built around the four curriculum threads.
  • Tracks how the pairings are going and reports active-pairing counts and meeting completion to the Secretary.
  • Draws on professional skills and life experience recorded on the stake resource list to build the mentor pool, and receives career and life-transition needs flagged by the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator.

Implementation Ideas

  • Use a simple mentor-application intake (background, availability, areas of experience) before pairing anyone.
  • Keep a pairing tracker: mentor, mentee, pairing date, last meeting date, and next scheduled meeting.
  • Flag any pairing with no contact in 45+ days for a personal check-in.
  • Give every mentor a one-page confidentiality reminder: keep mentoring conversations private, and refer safety, worthiness, or mental-health concerns to the Coordinator or a bishop.
  • Prioritize new pairings for YSAs without nearby family within their first 30 days in the pairing pool.

docs.title: Institute & Covenant Progression Liaison
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.8 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (works with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead)
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

This Liaison makes Institute the true hub of the Committee's work, boosting enrollment and clearing barriers like rides and scheduling for young single adults ages 18–35 (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 4B). Institute course topics are lined up with the stake's four curriculum threads wherever possible.

Key Responsibilities

  • Partners with institute faculty and the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead to boost enrollment and clear away barriers like rides and scheduling.
  • Lines up institute course topics with the stake's four curriculum threads wherever possible.
  • Sends institute enrollment numbers relevant to Education & Enrichment programming to the Secretary each month.
  • Shares institute course offerings with the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator and uses needs patterns to recommend courses that complement, rather than duplicate, stake workshops and firesides.

Implementation Ideas

  • Post a simple ride-share sign-up sheet each Institute term for anyone without transportation.
  • Meet with Institute faculty each term to compare the course catalog against the current curriculum thread.
  • Track enrollment by ward so under-enrolled wards get a targeted, personal-invite push.
  • Personally invite every newly identified less-active or new-move-in YSA to at least one Institute class within their first 30 days.
  • Share a short monthly enrollment snapshot (numbers plus trend) with the Secretary before the Committee Core meeting.

Reference

  • General Handbook 14, "Single Members" — https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/14-single-members?lang=eng

docs.title: Learning & Enrichment Coordinator
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.9 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (a stake calling under the direction of the stake presidency and the assigned high councilor, the Priesthood Co-Chair)
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

This Coordinator is the Committee's needs-and-resources hub. The role is not just event planning — it is a way of ministering: gathering members' interests, talents, and needs and connecting them with people and resources that can bless them, so every offering helps members feel seen, strengthens faith, and supports covenant keeping.

Key Responsibilities

  • Identifies member interests, talents, skills, and unmet needs through a member survey, interviews, and input from bishoprics, Relief Society, Elders Quorum, and ward YSA leaders.
  • Keeps the stake-wide resource list of willing teachers, presenters, and subject-matter experts, and shares it with every Coordinator.
  • Recommends 3 to 5 topics each planning cycle that fit stake priorities and the current curriculum thread, each paired with a Christ-centered framing.
  • Plans stake firesides and needs-driven pilot classes, and hands those that prove useful to the Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator so the two seats never compete.
  • Reports needs patterns, attendance, feedback, and recommended future topics to the Secretary and the Co-Chairs.

Coordination with the Committee

  • Co-Chairs: set scope, survey approval, and reporting expectations at the start of the term; deliver a needs-and-topics summary each planning cycle.
  • Workshop & Seminar Series Coordinator: meet monthly in the Needs & Resources Huddle to align calendars, avoid duplicate topics, and hand off proven pilots and presenters.
  • Enrichment Night Producer and Discussion Group Coordinator: supply needs-based topics, speakers, and study interests from the survey and resource list.
  • Small-Group Facilitator and Mentorship Pairing Coordinators: share members with teaching, facilitation, or professional skills; receive themes and needs back without names.
  • Institute Liaison, Secretary, and Advisor Couples: share needs patterns for course alignment, provide monthly metrics for the dashboard, and invite advisor skills for the resource list.

Implementation Ideas

  • Ask every ward and stake leader, "What are the most common needs or gaps you see among our YSA members?" and combine the answers with survey results.
  • Build the resource list as a simple spreadsheet with columns for topic, audience, suggested presenter, cost, location, and spiritual purpose — reviewed each planning cycle.
  • Plan one pilot first, such as a "Faith and Future" workshop with a short devotional, a practical class, and a testimony-bearing close; promote it well and gather feedback.
  • Track a few metrics each cycle: members surveyed, top needs, resources added, events held, and attendance.

docs.title: Committee Secretary / Metrics Recorder
docs.text:
Committee Core — Tier 1 · Coordinator

Section 4.10 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs
  • Selection & Term: Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the YSA Co-Chairs; extended as a calling or formal assignment, interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered.

Purpose

The Secretary sits at the hub of the reporting chain, consolidating every Coordinator's numbers into a single dashboard and a monthly stewardship report for the Co-Chairs (Gathering Plan, Part 4, Section 8; charter Section 6.1–6.2). Meeting notes, rosters, and attendance data are Church records and are handled accordingly.

Key Responsibilities

  • Takes minutes and tracks action items for every Committee Core meeting.
  • Pulls together the monthly attendance, facilitator, workshop, discussion-group, mentorship, and needs-gathering dashboard from data each Coordinator provides.
  • Drafts the monthly enrichment stewardship report for the Co-Chairs to deliver to the Executive Co-Chairs.
  • Keeps track of the Committee roster, term dates, and any upcoming turnover or succession needs.
  • Records the Learning & Enrichment topic pipeline and related action items in the minutes, and adds needs-gathering metrics to the dashboard.

Implementation Ideas

  • Build one shared dashboard (spreadsheet or shared document) with a tab per Coordinator so data rolls up automatically.
  • Send each Coordinator a same-day-of-month reminder to submit their numbers before the report is due.
  • Store minutes and the roster/term-date tracker in an access-limited shared folder, so records stay available only to those with a need to know.
  • Flag any Coordinator whose term ends within 90 days at the top of the roster so succession planning starts early.
  • Use the Attendance & Participation / Facilitator & Mentor Health / Covenant Progression / Member Needs & Resources / Look-Ahead / Risks & Needs framework as a fixed checklist every month so nothing gets skipped.

docs.title: Married Couple Advisors
docs.text:
Standing Advisor Couples — non-voting · 2–3 couples

Section 4.11 of the Charter

  • Reports To: Advisory relationship to the Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (not a supervisory reporting line)
  • Selection & Term: Called by the stake presidency, following the orientation in A Guide for Married Couples Serving in the Boise YSA Stake; interviewed and set apart. Concurrent with assignment; no fixed rotation.

Purpose

Married couples serve this Committee as advisors, not leaders. They sit with the Co-Chairs to plan, join the Mentorship Pairing pool, and may be invited to speak on marriage, parenting, or career and financial topics — while young single adults plan, run, and teach every enrichment night, workshop, and discussion group.

Key Responsibilities

  • Sit with the Committee Core in planning meetings as counsel, not as chairs; share experience when asked or when the Spirit prompts, never as a directive to follow.
  • Serve in the Mentorship Pairing pool as mentors, and may be invited to speak in the Workshop & Seminar Series on marriage, parenting, or career and financial topics; share their skills for the stake resource list and suggest topics when the Learning & Enrichment Coordinator asks.
  • Attend enrichment nights, workshops, and discussion groups as guests and friends, there to be present, not to run the program; young adult facilitators greet, lead, and teach.
  • Coach and encourage Coordinators privately; if something needs correcting, do it specifically, kindly, and away from the group, per the Guide for Married Couples.

Implementation Ideas

  • Complete the First 30 Days orientation from the Guide for Married Couples and meet the supporting high councilor before your first Committee meeting.
  • Sit toward the back or side at events rather than the front, so facilitators are clearly seen as leading.
  • Keep a private, running note of encouragement or coaching points for each Coordinator and share it one-on-one, never in the group setting.
  • Offer your specific expertise (career, marriage, finances, parenting) to the Workshop Coordinator ahead of each quarterly calendar build.
  • Volunteer for the Mentorship Pairing pool early each cycle so the Coordinator can pair you before the roster fills.

docs.title: Facilitator and Mentor Network (Tier 2)
docs.text:
Facilitators · Presenters · Discussion Hosts · Mentors — 15–25, seasonal

Section 4.12 of the Charter

  • Reports To: The relevant Coordinator (Small-Group Facilitator, Workshop & Seminar, Discussion Group, or Mentorship Pairing)
  • Selection & Term: Recruited by the relevant Coordinator each curriculum cycle or season; an informal assignment, not a calling, unless the ward extends one separately. One curriculum cycle or season, renewable.

Purpose

Network members carry the four curriculum threads into every small group, workshop, and mentoring relationship (Gathering Plan, Part 4). They are not standing Committee members — they train, attend assigned sessions, and report back to their Coordinator each time.

Key Responsibilities

  • Complete training on teaching standards and confidentiality within two weeks of being assigned.
  • Attend every session they're assigned to and immediately report attendance and participation notes to the Coordinator afterward.
  • Bring any individual needs, concerns, or opportunities to the Coordinator rather than handling sensitive situations on one's own.

Implementation Ideas

  • Schedule your training within your first week of being asked to serve, rather than waiting for a reminder.
  • Keep a short note (notebook or app) after every session: who was new, who seemed to need follow-up, who to watch for next time.
  • Learn the referral pathway before your first session: personal concerns go to your Coordinator; anything involving safety, worthiness, or a mental-health crisis goes straight to a bishop.
  • Arrive 10 minutes early to greet people as they come in, especially anyone arriving alone.
  • Ask your Coordinator for the current curriculum thread ahead of each session so your teaching or discussion ties back to it.

docs.text: Prepared for the Boise Idaho YSA Stake YSA Council — October 2026

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This charter operationalizes Section 9 of the Gathering Plan — "Organization, Roles, and Accountability." It defines how the Stake YSA Council is organized, staffed, and held accountable for executing the plan day-to-day, and serves as the executive co-chairs' standing reference and onboarding guide.

Total Council Members Executive Council Seats Ward Reps (6 Wards) Priority Program Areas 25 13 12 4

docs.title: Who Does What
docs.text:
• Stake Presidency — sets vision and priorities; approves the Gathering Plan, budget, and major changes; calls/releases Council leaders; receives regular reports and offers guidance.
  • Stake YSA Council — owns execution across Activities, Athletics, Education & Enrichment, and Outreach/Shepherding; builds the calendar, manages the approved budget, and reports progress on a regular schedule.

docs.title: Council Structure
docs.text: Group Composition Executive Council 13 seats, all YSAs: Executive Co-Chairs (RS President; High Councilor); Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads (2); Activities, Athletics, and Education & Enrichment Co-Chairs (2 each); Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead; Communications & Calendar Lead; Council Secretary/Metrics Recorder. Ward Representatives 2 per ward: Rep A (Ward Elders Quorum Presidency Counselor) covers outreach for EQ brothers; Rep B (Ward RS Presidency Counselor) covers activity attendance/follow-up for RS sisters — an extension of their existing calling. Both sit on the Full Council. Terms Co-chairs and ward reps serve as long as they hold their base calling; Leads/Secretary serve 12–18 months, staggered, with a 4–6 week handoff overlap.

docs.title: Meeting Rhythm & Reporting
docs.text:
Meeting Frequency Purpose Executive Council Weekly (first 90 days), then biweekly Review numbers, plan next 2–4 weeks, work shepherding assignments Full Council Monthly Coordinate calendar, cross-ward invitations, training Stake Presidency Report Monthly Written + verbal update on highlights, risks, decisions needed Quarterly Priority Review Quarterly Deeper look at progress on the four priorities Belonging Survey Review Twice yearly Review survey results and act on findings Annual Planning Retreat Yearly (Sept/Oct) Look back and build next year's calendar and goals

Reporting flow: Ward Reps → Leads → Secretary (dashboard & monthly report) → Co-Chairs → Stake Presidency.

docs.title: Decision Guide
docs.text:
• Council decides: program content, calendar/event design, and duty rotation within the Council.
  • Council recommends, Stake Presidency approves: new signature events or spending beyond budget; extending or releasing callings.
  • Flagged immediately: building-use/priesthood conflicts and sensitive personal or pastoral situations go straight to bishops and the stake presidency.

docs.title: First 90 Days
docs.text:
• Weeks 1–2: confirm charter, clean up roster, identify leads.
  • Weeks 2–4: call/set apart leads and secretary; bishoprics identify the assigned EQ & RS counselors as ward reps.
  • Weeks 4–6: first Executive Council meeting; belonging survey launched.
  • Weeks 6–8: first Full Council meeting; 90-day calendar published.
  • Weeks 8–12: first monthly report and first activities delivered under the new structure.

Bottom line

A 25-member, YSA-run Council — 13 executive seats plus ward reps — with a steady meeting rhythm and single reporting line keeps the stake presidency informed and able to guide through vision and approval, while the Council holds real ownership, clear accountability, and a direct connection to the plan's four priorities.

docs.title: 1. Purpose of This Document
docs.text:
The Boise, Idaho, YSA Stake Gathering Plan outlines the stake's vision and strategy for outreach to and gathering of Young Single Adults (YSAs). This charter builds on Section 9 of that plan — "Organization, Roles, and Accountability" — by detailing how the YSA Council is organized, staffed, and held accountable for executing the plan day to day. The Gathering Plan explains what needs to happen. This document explains who's responsible, how many people are needed, how the work is divided, and how the Council reports back to the stake presidency.

This is intended to be approved by the stake presidency and to serve as the YSA Council co-chairs' everyday reference and onboarding guide.

docs.title: 2. Who Does What: Stake Presidency and the Council
docs.text:
The Gathering Plan draws a clear line between designing the plan and carrying it out. This charter keeps that line clear:

Who What They Do Stake Presidency Sets the vision and priorities, and approves the Gathering Plan and any major changes to it. Calls and releases the Council's co-chairs, leads, and specialists. Approves the yearly budget and any spending outside it. Gets regular updates and offers guidance, counsel, and correction — steps in on building-use conflicts, doctrinal questions, and sensitive pastoral situations. Stake YSA Council Fully owns putting the Gathering Plan into action across all three program areas (Activities, Athletics, Education & Enrichment) plus the outreach and shepherding work under Priority 1. Builds the calendar, staffs every event and program, tracks attendance and outreach, and adjusts as needed. Manages the approved budget and oversees the volunteers and callings under the Council. Reports progress, risks, and needs to the stake presidency on a regular schedule (Section 6).

What the Council can decide on its own:

  • Program content, activity themes, and the monthly/quarterly calendar within the four priorities.
  • Who does what and how duties rotate within the Council and its Committees.
  • Day-to-day outreach, invitations, and follow-up.

What needs stake presidency approval:

  • Any new calling, release, or change to who sits on the Council.
  • Spending beyond the approved budget, or moving money between major categories.
  • Building-schedule conflicts with priesthood or other stake/ward activities.
  • Sensitive personal situations (mental health crisis, worthiness concerns, safety issues) — these go straight to the bishops and stake presidency rather than being handled within the Council.

docs.title: 3. How the Council Is Set Up
docs.text: The Council operates on two levels: an executive team responsible for outcomes and a network of ward reps who carry the plan into every ward.

docs.title: 3.1 Executive Council (the core team)
docs.text:
Thirteen seats, all filled by Young Single Adults, each person owning one clear piece of the Gathering Plan:

Seat Handles Advisors Sister Co-Chair — Stake YSA Relief Society President Co-leads the Council; sets the shepherding tone; sister-specific outreach and covenant progression Stake Presidency Priesthood Co-Chair — YSA High Councilor Co-leads the Council; priesthood correlation; main link to the stake presidency. Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Sister) "Know Them by Name" for sister YSAs, sister Gathering Specialists, less-active rescue, move-in welcome; works with Ward Rep B (RS) Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Priesthood) "Know Them by Name" for brother YSAs, brother Gathering Specialists, less-active rescue, move-in welcome; works with Ward Rep A (EQ); combined outreach report Activities Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood) Stake Activities Committee — social, service, adventure, and signature events Activities Committee Co-Chair (Sister) Stake Activities Committee — social, service, adventure, and signature events Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood) Stake Athletics Committee — open play, leagues, inter-stake and outdoor events Athletics Committee Co-Chair (Sister) Stake Athletics Committee — open play, leagues, inter-stake and outdoor events Education & Enrichment Committee Co-Chair (Priesthood) Enrichment nights, workshops, discussion groups, mentor pairing Education & Enrichment Committee Co-Chair (Sister) Enrichment nights, workshops, discussion groups, mentor pairing Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead (Institute Council President) Institute partnership, temple nights/recommends, covenant pathway tracking (Priority 4) Communications & Calendar Lead Master calendar, invitation rhythm, multi-channel messaging, story-sharing Council Secretary / Metrics Recorder Minutes, attendance and outreach data, dashboards, drafting reports to the stake presidency

docs.title: 3.2 Ward Representatives
docs.text: Following the Gathering Plan, each ward calls or assigns two YSA reps. They focus on outreach and invitations, working with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads (Rep A with the Priesthood Co-Lead, Rep B with the Sister Co-Lead); running activities, tracking attendance, and following up; and, as needed, working with the Activities, Athletics, and Enrichment leads. Ward reps sit on the Full Council, serve as the ward's point of contact for each program, and ensure that their ward's YSAs are known, invited, and followed up with.

docs.title: 3.3 Council Size
docs.text:
Total Council size = 13 (Executive Council) + 12 (Ward Representatives)

Wards in the Stake Ward Reps Executive Council Total 6 12 13 25

docs.title: 4. Roles: Who's Responsible for What
docs.text: Each Executive Council seat below is written as a standing role description. Use these as-is when calling or briefing Council members. (Full role cards — including Purpose, Implementation Ideas, and References — appear above under "Role Descriptions"; the summaries below reproduce the charter document's own Section 4 text.)

docs.title: 4.1 Executive Co-Chair — Stake YSA Relief Society President
docs.text:
Reports to: Stake Presidency (together with the Priesthood Co-Chair)

  • Co-leads the Executive Council and Full Council; co-chairs every meeting.
  • Champions the "belonging audit" and the twice-a-year belonging survey, and follows through on what it finds.
  • Makes sure sister YSAs — especially less-active and new-to-the-area sisters — are personally known and cared for, working with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Sister).
  • Partners with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead.
  • Represents the Council to Relief Society.

What success looks like: Belonging survey completion and trends; sister participation in "Know Them by Name."

docs.title: 4.2 Executive Co-Chair — YSA High Councilor
docs.text:
Reports to: Stake Presidency (together with the Sister Co-Chair)

  • Co-leads the Executive Council and Full Council; carries the stake presidency's delegated priesthood oversight.
  • Is the main point of contact with the stake presidency, including monthly and quarterly reports.
  • Coordinates with bishops on building use, priesthood correlation, and sensitive referrals.
  • Reviews and recommends any Council calling changes to the stake presidency.
  • Makes sure every program stays Christ-centered and doctrine-first.

What success looks like: Monthly reports delivered on time; issues resolved within a week.

docs.title: 4.3 Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Sister)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs (works most closely with the Sister Co-Chair)

  • Co-owns the "Know Them by Name" contact system with the Priesthood Co-Lead, with primary responsibility for every sister YSA on the roster.
  • Coordinates sister Gathering Specialists; teams up with ward Relief Society presidencies and Ward Rep B on less-active rescue among sisters.
  • Runs the welcome plan for newly arrived and newly turned-18 sisters, including returned missionaries (contact within 7 days, invite within 14).
  • Keeps the sister portion of the master roster current — active, less-active, non-attending, and new move-in YSAs.
  • Partners with the Sister Co-Chair on sister-specific outreach and on following through with belonging survey findings; sends sister outreach numbers to the Priesthood Co-Lead for the combined monthly report.

What success looks like: Percent of sisters on the roster contacted each month; sister move-ins reached within 7 days.

docs.title: 4.4 Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs (works most closely with the Priesthood Co-Chair)

  • Co-owns the "Know Them by Name" contact system with the Sister Co-Lead, with primary responsibility for every brother YSA on the roster.
  • Coordinates brother Gathering Specialists; teams up with ward elders quorum presidencies and Ward Rep A on less-active rescue among brothers, including ministering coordination.
  • Runs the welcome plan for newly arrived and newly turned-18 brothers, including returned missionaries (contact within 7 days, invite within 14).
  • Keeps the brother portion of the master roster current, and reconciles the combined roster with the Sister Co-Lead each month.
  • Sends the combined outreach numbers to the Secretary each month for the dashboard; routes any referral that needs a bishop through the Priesthood Co-Chair.

What success looks like: Percent of brothers on the roster contacted each month; brother move-ins reached within 7 days; combined outreach report delivered on time.

docs.title: 4.5 Activities Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-chairs every Category Lead huddle and Full Activities Committee meeting.
  • Sets the standard for making sure everyone feels included and welcome — greeters, name tags, mixing people from different wards.
  • Sets and reviews how Connection Hosts are recruited and trained, together with Category Leads and Ward Activity Representatives.
  • Works with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads to make sure less-active and new-move-in YSAs get personally invited.
  • Runs the after-event debriefs with each Category Lead and Activity Lead.

What success looks like: How many 48-hour follow-ups actually happen, and how many newcomers come back.

docs.title: 4.6 Activities Co-Chair (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-chairs every Category Lead huddle and Full Activities Committee meeting.
  • Keeps the six-week planning board up to date, working with the Communications & Calendar Lead.
  • Confirms Activity Lead assignments that Category Leads propose, at least six weeks before each event.
  • Manages the Activities Committee budget and sorts out any scheduling conflicts between categories.
  • Sends the monthly attendance and newcomer report to the YSA Council.

What success looks like: Activities happening on time and at a good standard every month, and staying within budget.

docs.title: 4.7 Athletics Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-chairs the committee with the Priesthood Co-Chair, sharing full ownership of the calendar and program quality.
  • Makes sure every league, open-play night, and tournament is designed so everyone feels included, welcome, and belongs.
  • Works with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads to make sure less-active and new-move-in YSAs get personally invited.
  • Coordinates recruiting and training Connection Hosts with the Ward Athletics Representatives.
  • Tracks weekly attendance, absentee follow-up, and less-active/non-member turnout alongside the Priesthood Co-Lead.

What success looks like: How many 48-hour follow-ups actually happen, and how many newcomers come back.

docs.title: 4.8 Athletics Co-Chair (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-chairs the committee with the Sister Co-Chair, and oversees the Sport Commissioners, Team Captains, and Connection Hosts.
  • Owns facility scheduling, equipment inventory, and safety standards for all athletics.
  • Builds and runs the season calendar (open play, leagues, tournaments, inter-stake and outdoor events) and gets it to the Communications & Calendar Lead at least 60 days ahead.
  • Makes sure every league and open-play night includes the "More Than a Game" spiritual message and the written sportsmanship standard.
  • Recruits, briefs, and checks in with Sport Commissioners each season, and represents the Committee at the Stake YSA Council meeting.

What it looks like when it's working: attendance trending up week over week; absentees contacted within 48 hours; seasons starting on time.

docs.title: 4.9 Education & Enrichment Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-leads the Education & Enrichment Committee; co-chairs every Committee Core meeting with the Priesthood Executive Co-Chair.
  • Runs the Monthly Stake Enrichment Night and rotates through the four curriculum threads over the year, together with the Priesthood Co-Chair.
  • Champions sister-specific facilitator and mentor recruiting, and makes sure small groups are set up so no one sits alone.
  • Represents the Committee at the monthly YSA Council meeting alongside the Priesthood Co-Chair.
  • Makes sure every enrichment night ends with a specific invitation to take a covenant step.

Success metric: Monthly enrichment attendance and trend; facilitators trained per cycle.

docs.title: 4.10 Education & Enrichment Co-Chair (Priesthood)
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Co-leads the Education & Enrichment Committee; carries the Committee's reporting relationship with the YSA Council Executive Co-Chairs.
  • Coordinates the Workshop/Seminar series and keeps it aligned with the Institute, drawing on stake members' expertise.
  • Reviews Committee coordinator changes and recommends them to the YSA Council Co-Chairs.
  • Makes sure Christ-centered framing and doctrine-first teaching standards are upheld across every enrichment night, workshop, and discussion group.
  • Delivers the monthly enrichment stewardship report to the YSA Council Co-Chairs, prepared by the Secretary.

Success metric: On-time monthly reports; teaching-standards compliance across all sessions.

docs.title: 4.11 Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead — Institute Council President
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Partners with Institute faculty to boost enrollment and remove barriers (rides, scheduling).
  • Owns the covenant pathway map (attend → connect → institute → temple → calling → mission/marriage) for people being tracked.
  • Runs the temple recommend campaign and coordinates stake temple nights and group temple trips.
  • Lines up institute course topics with the stake's four curriculum threads where it makes sense.
  • Reports institute enrollment and temple recommend numbers to the Secretary.

What success looks like: Institute enrollment rate, temple recommend holders, and temple night attendance.

docs.title: 4.12 Communications & Calendar Lead
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Owns the one shared stake calendar used by every ward.
  • Runs the invitation flow for every event: personal invite → text reminder → group announcement.
  • Creates outreach materials (announcements, group texts, graphics) for the other leads.
  • Gathers stories — testimonies and experiences from leaders and YSAs — to keep momentum going.
  • Keeps the Council's communication channels (group chat, shared calendar, contact lists) up to date.

What success looks like: Calendar published 60+ days out; invite chain completed for each event.

docs.title: 4.13 Council Secretary / Metrics Recorder
docs.text:
Reports to: Executive Co-Chairs

  • Takes minutes and tracks action items for every Executive and Full Council meeting.
  • Puts together the monthly dashboard using data from each lead.
  • Drafts the monthly report and quarterly review packet for the stake presidency (Section 6).
  • Tracks the Council roster, term dates, and upcoming turnover.
  • Runs the twice-a-year belonging survey and compiles the results.

What success looks like: Reports delivered on time; dashboard is accurate and complete.

docs.title: 4.14 Ward Representatives (two per ward)
docs.text:
Reports to: Council Leads for the work; their bishopric liaison for anything pastoral

  • Counselor in Ward EQ Presidency (Rep A), Counselor in Ward RS Presidency (Rep B).[^1]
  • Outreach: identifies ward members in their respective organizations to contact, extend personal invitations, and runs "Know Them by Name" contacts for that ward.
  • Activities/Attendance: tracks ward attendance at activities, athletics, and enrichment nights for their respective organizations; leads 48-hour follow-up for newcomers and no-shows in that ward/organization.
  • Both attend the monthly Full Council meeting and bring stake-level assignments back to their ward.
  • Both raise ward-level needs and concerns up to the relevant Lead.

What success looks like: Ward-level contact and follow-up rate; ward attendance trend.

docs.title: 5. How People Are Chosen and How Long They Serve
docs.text:
Seat How They Get There Term Co-Chairs Already called as YSA High Councilor and Stake YSA Relief Society President; no separate calling needed. As long as they hold that calling Leads, Co-Leads & Secretary Nominated by the Co-Chairs with input from the stake presidency; called or formally assigned ("Stake YSA Gathering Specialist – [role]"); interviewed and set apart. 12–18 months, staggered Ward Representatives Already called as Elders Quorum Presidency Counselor and Counselor in Ward Relief Society Presidency; no separate calling needed. As long as they hold that calling

Stagger terms so no more than half of the Council turns over at once. Give outgoing and incoming leads a 4–6 week overlap for the handoff, since the YSA population changes often. Where a role is shared by two co-leads or co-chairs, stagger their terms so at least one experienced partner stays in place.

[^1]: Because this is a YSA stake, its entire population is young single adults. The General Handbook provision that lets an elders quorum or Relief Society president assign one counselor to focus specifically on young single adults (General Handbook 8.3.1 and 9.3.1, referencing 14.1.2.2) is written for a geographic ward that also serves married and older members. In this stake, there is no such other population to divide attention from — every EQ and RS counselor already serves an entirely young-single-adult organization. Rep A and Rep B's Ward Rep duties are therefore an operational extension of a responsibility the Handbook already assigns them, not a new or competing calling. No additional YSA-focused counselor assignment is needed on top of this Charter's Ward Rep structure.

docs.title: 6. Meetings and Reporting
docs.text: Meeting How Often Who Comes What It's For What Comes Out of It Executive Council Meeting Weekly for the first 90 days, then every other week Co-Chairs, Leads, Secretary A spiritual thought and prayer for specific people; review the numbers; plan the next 2–4 weeks; work through cross-program issues; seek guidance for specific YSAs by name; line up shepherding assignments Minutes and action items; updated rescue and shepherding list Full Council Meeting Monthly Executive Council + all Ward Reps Coordinate the calendar; plan cross-ward invitations; train; hear updates from the wards. Updated master calendar; ward assignments. Stake Presidency Report Monthly Co-Chairs (+ a Lead if needed) and the Stake Presidency A short written report plus a verbal update on highlights, risks, and any decisions needed Approved next steps; resource decisions Quarterly Priority Review Quarterly Executive Council + Stake Presidency A deeper look at progress on the four priorities and all the numbers Calendar and program adjustments Belonging Survey Review Twice a year Full Council + Stake Presidency Review the belonging survey results and act on what it shows Program adjustments Annual Planning Retreat Yearly (Sept/Oct) Full Council + Stake Presidency Look back at the year and build next year's calendar Year-two calendar and goals

docs.title: 6.1 How Information Flows
docs.text:
Information flows in one consistent line so nothing gets lost between the wards and the stake presidency:

  1. Ward reps track and report attendance, contacts, and follow-up at the ward level.
  2. Leads pull that ward data together with their own program data and bring it to the Executive Council meeting.
  3. The Secretary combines all the leads' reports into one dashboard and puts together the monthly report.
  4. The Co-Chairs review it, add context and any requests, and send it to the Stake Presidency.

docs.title: 6.2 Monthly Report Template
docs.text:
The Secretary drafts this every month for the Co-Chairs to pass along to the stake presidency. Keep it to one page, following the Gathering Plan's measurement framework (Section 10):

  • Attendance & Participation — activities, athletics, and enrichment turnout compared to last month and to the roster.
  • Outreach & Rescue — percent of roster personally contacted; less-active visits; new move-ins welcomed on schedule.
  • Covenant Progression — institute enrollment, temple recommend holders, reactivations, baptisms, and callings accepted.
  • What's Coming — the next 60 days on the calendar and the support that's needed.
  • Risks, Needs & Decisions — anything that needs stake presidency input or approval.

docs.title: 7. Decision Guide: What Needs Stake Presidency Approval
docs.text: Decision Council's Role Stake Presidency's Role Program content, calendar, and event design Decides Kept informed Assignments and duty rotation within the Council Decides Kept informed A new signature event or spending beyond budget Recommends Approves Extending or releasing callings/assignments Recommends Approves and sets apart Building-use or priesthood scheduling conflicts Coordinates Resolves conflicts Sensitive personal or pastoral situations Flags right away Handles with the bishops

docs.title: 8. How the Council Works Together
docs.text:
• Every meeting opens and closes with prayer, and starts with a short spiritual thought tied to one of the four priorities.
  • Conversations about specific people (rescue efforts, sensitive needs) stay within the Council and are shared with bishops only when they need to know.
  • Decisions are made by consensus among the Co-Chairs and the relevant Leads. If something can't be resolved, it goes to the stake presidency within a week rather than sitting unsettled.
  • Leads are expected at Executive Council meetings. If a Lead can't make it, a substitute (a deputy or Ward Rep) comes in their place.
  • Every Council member holds to the same "on-ramp, not destination" standard the Gathering Plan sets for activities — the Council tries to model belonging and purpose in its own meetings, the same way it wants to create that for YSAs.

docs.title: 9. Onboarding, Training, and Handoffs
docs.text:
• New Council members get a starter packet: this charter, the Gathering Plan, the current dashboard, and a handoff document from whoever had the role before them.
  • New Leads shadow their predecessor for one full meeting cycle before taking over fully, whenever the timing allows for overlap.
  • Each Lead keeps a living handoff document (contacts, vendor/venue info, open items, lessons learned) updated all along — not just at turnover.
  • Ward Reps are trained by their Lead counterpart within two weeks of starting, covering the invitation chain, follow-up expectations, and how to report data.

docs.title: 10. First 90 Days: Getting Started
docs.text:
Timeframe Milestones Weeks 1–2 Co-chairs confirm the charter with the stake presidency, clean up the YSA roster, and identify lead candidates. Weeks 2–4 Leads and Secretary called/assigned and set apart; ward bishoprics asked to identify two ward reps each (the EQ & RS counselors who have been assigned). Weeks 4–6 First Executive Council meeting; reporting templates and dashboard set up; belonging survey launched. Weeks 6–8 First Full Council meeting; ward reps trained; "Know Them by Name" assignments handed out; 90-day calendar published. Weeks 8–12 First monthly report delivered to the stake presidency; first quarterly review scheduled; first stake activity, league season, and enrichment night run under the new setup.

This timeline lines up with Phase 1 and the start of Phase 2 of the Gathering Plan's implementation timeline (Section 13), so the Council and the plan move forward together.

docs.title: 11. Summary
docs.text: This charter establishes a Council for the Boise YSA Stake, fully run by Young Single Adults and co-led by the YSA High Councilor and the Stake YSA Relief Society President. It has thirteen executive seats, each responsible for one clear piece of the Gathering Plan, plus a network of ward reps who carry the plan into every ward. A steady meeting rhythm and a single reporting line keep the stake presidency informed and able to guide through vision and approval — without managing the day-to-day — while the Council has real ownership, clear accountability, and a direct connection back to the plan's four priorities.

docs.title: Executive Co-Chair — Stake YSA Relief Society President
docs.text:
Executive Council — Co-Chair (Sister)

  • Reports To: Stake Presidency, together with the Priesthood Executive Co-Chair.
  • Positions Needed: One (1) — Executive Council seat.

Purpose

The Sister Co-Chair shares full leadership of the YSA Council with the Priesthood Co-Chair, co-running every Executive and Full Council meeting. She champions belonging for every sister in YSA — especially less-active and new-to-the-area sisters — and ensures the Council's work stays personal, not just programmatic.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-leads the Executive Council and Full Council; co-chairs every meeting.
  • Champions the "belonging audit" and the twice-a-year belonging survey, and follows through on what it finds.
  • Makes sure sister YSAs — especially less-active and new-to-the-area sisters — are personally known and cared for, working with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Sister).
  • Partners with the Gathering Place & Covenant Progression Lead.
  • Represents the Council to Relief Society.

What success looks like

Belonging survey completion and trends; sister participation in "Know Them by Name."

Implementation Ideas

  • Set a standing 15-minute check-in with the Priesthood Co-Chair before every Executive Council meeting to align the agenda.
  • Launch the twice-a-year belonging survey as a short 5-question online form, then build a personal follow-up call list for anyone who reports feeling disconnected.
  • Keep a running list of sister YSAs (less-active or new-to-area) and review it monthly with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Sister).
  • Rotate a short visit to each ward's Relief Society meeting over the year to stay visible and gather feedback firsthand.
  • Bring specific names, not just numbers, into every Executive Council discussion about sisters who need outreach.

Reference

  • Gathering Plan / Charter: Gathering Plan, Part 1, Section 9 — "Who's Doing What."
  • General Handbook: chapter 9, "Relief Society," on the Relief Society president's role of leading efforts in God's work of salvation and serving on councils. (View chapter)
  • General Handbook: chapter 14, "Single Members," on the stake young single adult committee and its co-leaders. (View chapter)

docs.title: Executive Co-Chair — YSA High Councilor
docs.text:
Executive Council — Co-Chair (Priesthood)

  • Reports To: Stake Presidency, together with the Sister Executive Co-Chair.
  • Positions Needed: One (1) — Executive Council seat.

Purpose

The Priesthood Co-Chair shares leadership of the YSA Council with the Sister Co-Chair and assumes the stake presidency's delegated priesthood oversight. He serves as the Council's primary line of accountability to the stake presidency and ensures every program remains Christ-centered and doctrine-first.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-leads the Executive Council and Full Council; carries the stake presidency's delegated priesthood oversight.
  • Is the main point of contact with the stake presidency, including monthly and quarterly reports.
  • Coordinates with bishops on building use, priesthood correlation, and sensitive referrals.
  • Reviews and recommends any Council calling changes to the stake presidency.
  • Makes sure every program stays Christ-centered and doctrine-first.

What success looks like

Monthly reports delivered on time; issues resolved within a week.

Implementation Ideas

  • Put a recurring calendar hold the same week every month for the stake presidency report, built from the Secretary's dashboard.
  • Keep a simple bishop-contact log for building use and priesthood correlation issues, and close each item within a week.
  • Bring a one-page Council calling roster to stake council meetings to flag any upcoming vacancy or change that needs approval.
  • Open each Executive Council meeting with a short doctrine-centered thought tied to one of the Gathering Plan's four priorities.
  • Track "issues resolved within a week" on the same tracker the Secretary uses for the monthly dashboard.

Reference

  • Gathering Plan / Charter: Gathering Plan, Part 1, Section 9 — "Who's Doing What."
  • General Handbook: chapter 6, "Stake Leadership," on high councilors' assignment to oversee YSA and elders quorum work under the stake presidency's direction. (View chapter)
  • General Handbook: chapter 14, "Single Members," on the assigned high councilor's role supporting the young single adult committee. (View chapter)

docs.title: Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Sister)
docs.text:
Executive Council — Co-Lead, Outreach & Shepherding

  • Reports To: Executive Co-Chairs (works most closely with the Sister Executive Co-Chair).
  • Positions Needed: One (1) — Executive Council seat.

Purpose

The Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Sister) co-owns the stake-level "Know Them by Name" contact system with the Priesthood Co-Lead and is primarily responsible for every sister YSA on the roster. She ensures every sister — active, less-active, non-attending, newly arrived, or newly turned 18, including returned missionaries — is personally known and welcomed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-owns the "Know Them by Name" contact system with the Priesthood Co-Lead, with primary responsibility for every sister YSA on the roster.
  • Coordinates sister Gathering Specialists; teams up with ward Relief Society presidencies and Ward Rep B on less-active rescue among sisters.
  • Runs the welcome plan for newly arrived and newly turned-18 sisters, including returned missionaries (contact within 7 days, invite within 14).
  • Keeps the sister portion of the master roster current — active, less-active, non-attending, and new move-in YSAs.
  • Partners with the Sister Co-Chair on sister-specific outreach and on following through with belonging survey findings; sends sister outreach numbers to the Priesthood Co-Lead for the combined monthly report.

What success looks like

Percent of sisters on the roster contacted each month; sister move-ins reached within 7 days.

Implementation Ideas

  • Keep the sister tab of the master roster segmented by active, less-active, non-attending, and new move-in, and review it monthly with each Ward Rep B.
  • Give every Ward Rep B a standing monthly "Know Them by Name" call list pulled straight from the sister roster.
  • Set an automatic 7-day/14-day reminder the same week a newly arrived sister, newly turned-18 sister, or returned missionary appears in ward records.
  • Hold a monthly 30-minute call with sister Gathering Specialists and ward Relief Society presidencies to trade challenges and best practices ahead of the Executive Council meeting.

Reference

docs.title: Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Priesthood)

Executive Council — Co-Lead, Outreach & Shepherding

  • Reports To: Executive Co-Chairs (works most closely with the Priesthood Executive Co-Chair).
  • Positions Needed: One (1) — Executive Council seat.

Purpose

The Outreach & Shepherding Co-Lead (Priesthood) co-owns the stake-level "Know Them by Name" contact system with the Sister Co-Lead and is primarily responsible for every brother YSA on the roster. He ensures every brother — active, less-active, non-attending, newly arrived, or newly turned 18, including returned missionaries — is personally known and welcomed. He reconciles the combined roster each month and delivers the combined outreach report that feeds the Council dashboard.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-owns the "Know Them by Name" contact system with the Sister Co-Lead, with primary responsibility for every brother YSA on the roster.
  • Coordinates brother Gathering Specialists; teams up with ward elders quorum presidencies and Ward Rep A on less-active rescue among brothers, including ministering coordination.
  • Runs the welcome plan for newly arrived and newly turned-18 brothers, including returned missionaries (contact within 7 days, invite within 14).
  • Keeps the brother portion of the master roster current, and reconciles the combined roster with the Sister Co-Lead each month.
  • Sends the combined outreach numbers to the Secretary each month for the dashboard; routes any referral that needs a bishop through the Priesthood Co-Chair.

What success looks like

Percent of brothers on the roster contacted each month; brother move-ins reached within 7 days; combined outreach report delivered on time.

Implementation Ideas

  • Keep the brother tab of the master roster segmented by active, less-active, non-attending, and new move-in, and review it monthly with each Ward Rep A.
  • Give every Ward Rep A a standing monthly "Know Them by Name" call list, and use quarterly ministering interviews as a key outreach data source.
  • Set an automatic 7-day/14-day reminder the same week a newly arrived brother, newly turned-18 brother, or returned missionary appears in ward records.
  • Meet monthly with the Sister Co-Lead to reconcile the combined roster before the numbers go to the Secretary, and flag any YSA who appears on neither list.
  • Send the combined outreach report to the Secretary by the same date every month (for example, the 25th), and pass any bishop-level referral to the Priesthood Co-Chair the same day it surfaces.

Reference

  • Gathering Plan / Charter: Gathering Plan, Part 1, Section 4 — "Priority 1: See and Love as God Does."
  • General Handbook: chapter 14, "Single Members," on leaders reaching out to single adults and including them in the work of the Church. (View chapter)
  • General Handbook: chapter 21, "Ministering," on discerning needs and providing Christlike love and follow-up. (View chapter)
  • General Handbook: chapter 8, "Elders Quorum," on elders quorum presidencies ministering to quorum members and coordinating ministering. (View chapter)

docs.title: Activities Co-Chair (Sister)
docs.text:
Executive Council — Co-Chair, Activities Committee

  • Reports To: Executive Co-Chairs.
  • Positions Needed: One (1) — Executive Council seat.

Purpose

The Activities Co-Chair (Sister) sets the tone for belonging at every Category Lead huddle and Full Activities Committee meeting, ensuring that greeters, name tags, and cross-ward mixing make every event feel like a place where newcomers and less-active YSAs feel personally invited and welcomed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-chairs every Category Lead huddle and Full Activities Committee meeting.
  • Sets the standard for making sure everyone feels included and welcome — greeters, name tags, mixing people from different wards.
  • Sets and reviews how Connection Hosts are recruited and trained, together with Category Leads and Ward Activity Representatives.
  • Works with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads to make sure less-active and new-move-in YSAs get personally invited.
  • Runs the after-event debriefs with each Category Lead and Activity Lead.

What success looks like

How many 48-hour follow-ups actually happen, and how many newcomers come back.

Implementation Ideas

  • Build a simple greeter/name-tag/cross-ward-mixing checklist that every Category Lead runs through before doors open.
  • Give Connection Hosts a one-page training card covering how to spot a newcomer and make the first introduction.
  • Ask the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads for a short list of less-active or new-move-in names before each event and personally text an invite to each one.
  • Run the after-event debrief within 48 hours and ask each Category Lead one question: "Who came for the first time, and did we follow up?"
  • Rotate which Category Lead hosts the monthly huddle so ownership of inclusion doesn't default to one committee.

Reference

  • Gathering Plan / Charter: Gathering Plan, Part 2, Section 5 — "Who's Running This."
  • General Handbook: chapter 20, "Activities," on stake activities requiring stake presidency approval and coordination through stake council. (View chapter)
  • General Handbook: chapter 14, "Single Members," on activities for young single adults taking place at ward, stake, or multistake level. (View chapter)

Executive Council — Co-Chair, Activities Committee

  • Reports To: Executive Co-Chairs.
  • Positions Needed: One (1) — Executive Council seat.

Purpose

The Activities Co-Chair (Priesthood) keeps the six-week planning board on schedule, confirms Activity Lead assignments early, and manages the budget so that every stake activity is delivered on time, to a high standard, and within its financial limits.

Key Responsibilities

  • Co-chairs every Category Lead huddle and Full Activities Committee meeting.
  • Keeps the six-week planning board up to date, working with the Communications & Calendar Lead.
  • Confirms Activity Lead assignments that Category Leads propose, at least six weeks before each event.
  • Manages the Activities Committee budget and sorts out any scheduling conflicts between categories.
  • Sends the monthly attendance and newcomer report to the YSA Council.

What success looks like

Activities happening on time and at a good standard every month, and staying within budget.

Implementation Ideas

  • Keep the six-week planning board as a single shared document with the Communications & Calendar Lead, updated every huddle.
  • Require Category Leads to propose their Activity Lead by six weeks out, then confirm in writing within 48 hours.
  • Track the Activities Committee budget in one running spreadsheet, reviewed at each Full Activities Committee meeting.
  • Flag any building-schedule or category-timing conflict the moment it appears — these need stake presidency approval before they're locked in.
  • Send the monthly attendance and newcomer report to the YSA Council on the same date every month, matching the Secretary's dashboard deadline.

Reference

Executive Council — Co-Chair, Athletics Committee

  • Reports To: Executive Co-Chairs.
  • Positions Needed: One (1) — Executive Council seat.

Purpose

The Athletics Co-Chair (Sister) shares ownership of the athletics calendar and program quality with the Priesthood Co-Chair, ensuring that every league night, open play, and tournament is designed so newcomers and less-active YSAs feel personally invited and never sit on the sidelines unnoticed.

  • Co-chairs the committee with the Priesthood Co-Chair, sharing full ownership of the calendar and program quality.
  • Makes sure every league, open-play night, and tournament is designed so everyone feels included, welcome, and belongs.
  • Works with the Outreach & Shepherding Co-Leads to make sure less-active and new-move-in YSAs get personally invited.
  • Coordinates recruiting and training Connection Hosts with the Ward Athletics Representatives.
  • Tracks weekly attendance, absentee follow-up, and less-active/non-member turnout alongside the Priesthood Co-Lead.

What success looks like

How many 48-hour follow-ups actually happen, and how many newcomers come back.

Implementation Ideas

  • Co-review the season calendar with the Priesthood Co-Chair monthly to keep ownership of quality shared, not siloed by sport.
  • Ask Ward Athletics Representatives for a short list of less-active or new-move-in names before each season starts.
  • Give Connection Hosts a one-page checklist for welcoming a new face at league night or open play.
  • Track weekly attendance and absentee follow-up on one shared sheet with the Priesthood Co-Chair, reviewed every Sunday evening.
  • Personally text-invite at least three less-active or new-move-in YSAs before each week's open play.

Reference
